title: Institutional Capacity and Documented COVID-19 Response Among Romanian Public Health Directorates: A Reproducible Cross-Sectional Comparative Analysis
abstract: Background: The COVID-19 pandemic exposed substantial differences in the capacity of local public health authorities to adapt, coordinate, communicate, engage communities, and sustain essential public health functions. Methods: We conducted a secondary, institution-level cross-sectional analysis of the verified analytic dataset for 20 Romanian Public Health Directorates (PHDs), representing 20 of 42 county-level territorial units. The file contained structural variables, eight binary COVID-19 response indicators, four normalized components, and an equal-weight composite capacity–response index, but no repeated annual observations, five-domain resilience scores, source-document matrix, or coder-reliability records. Comparisons between counties with university medical centers (CU; n = 10) and counties without them (FU; n = 10) used Mann–Whitney U and Fisher’s exact tests with Holm correction. Results: CU institutions served larger populations and had more employees, larger total budgets, higher budget per capita, more previous-crisis experience, more documented COVID-19 measures, and a higher exploratory composite index. Staffing density did not differ significantly. Vaccination-center involvement and communication/education were more frequently documented in CU institutions after multiplicity correction. Bucharest, Iași, and Cluj illustrate meaningful within-group variation despite a shared university-center context. Conclusions: The available data support descriptive evidence of institutional disparities associated with university-center context, but do not support causal claims, a longitudinal five-domain resilience model, or conclusions about digital maturity. The findings point to practical priorities for PHD–university medical-center collaboration, bidirectional community engagement, systematic after-action review, transparent national data collection, and future instrument validation.

title: Prophylactic vs Therapeutic Anticoagulation in Hospitalized Patients With COVID-19
abstract: Importance: Coagulopathy in the context of COVID-19 is a major threat due to deep vein thromboses and pulmonary embolisms. Objective: To assess whether therapeutic anticoagulation on top of standard of care (SOC) compared with prophylactic anticoagulation as part of SOC can improve objective patient-relevant end points. Design, Setting, and Participants: This prospective, assessor-blinded, multicenter, parallel-group (1:1), placebo-controlled, superiority randomized clinical trial (HERO-19) assessed patients with a confirmed diagnosis of COVID-19 who were hospitalized in an intensive care unit or non-intensive care ward at 1 of 10 university hospitals in Germany from November 12, 2020, to January 15, 2023. Data analysis was conducted after the final database lock in February 2024. Interventions: Patients were treated for 42 days. Patients enrolled in the experimental group received therapeutic anticoagulation using low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) body weight adapted during the hospital stay and oral anticoagulation using edoxaban, 60 mg daily, after being discharged from the hospital. Patients enrolled in the control group received prophylactic anticoagulation using LMWH as part of SOC while in the hospital and placebo after discharge. Main Outcomes and Measures: The primary end point was time to the first occurrence of all-cause mortality and/or venous thromboembolism and/or arterial thromboembolism within up to 42 days. Potential thromboembolic events were assessed by duplex ultrasonography of arms and legs at day 14 or discharge and day 42. The primary safety outcome was major and clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding according to International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis classification. Results: A total of 139 patients (mean [SD] age, 58.4 [13.7] years; 93 [67%] male and 46 [33%] female) were included in the study. Of these, 71 patients (51%) were randomized to prophylactic anticoagulation group, whereas 68 (49%) were randomized to the therapeutic anticoagulation group. The primary outcome occurred in 14 of 67 patients (21%; 2.31 incidence per patient-year) assigned to therapeutic anticoagulation and 20 of 70 (29%; 3.37 incidence per patient-year) assigned to prophylactic anticoagulation (primary end point assessment not available for 2 patients) with primary end point assessment (hazard ratio, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.38-1.48; P = .40). In the per-protocol analysis, the hazard ratio was 0.66 (95% CI, 0.32-1.37; P = .26). A total of 7 bleeding events occurred in the intervention group, whereas 6 bleeding events occurred in the control group. Conclusions and Relevance: In patients hospitalized with COVID-19, in-hospital therapeutic anticoagulation with LMWH followed by edoxaban to day 42 did not statistically significantly reduce death and/or thromboembolic events compared with prophylactic anticoagulation followed by placebo. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04542408.

title: PROGNOSTIC VALUE OF COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY AND INFLAMMATORY BIOMARKERS IN HOSPITALIZED PATIENTS WITH COVID-19 VALOR PRONÓSTICO DE LA TOMOGRAFÍA COMPUTARIZADA Y LOS BIOMARCADORES INFLAMATORIOS EN PACIENTES HOSPITALIZADOS CON COVID-19 VALOR PROGNÓSTICO DA TOMOGRAFIA COMPUTADORIZADA E DE BIOMARCADORES INFLAMATÓRIOS EM PACIENTES HOSPITALIZADOS COM COVID-19
abstract: To evaluate the association of thoracic imaging findings, clinical severity, and comorbidities with outcomes in patients with COVID-19, and to determine the discriminatory performance of inflammatory biomarkers and blood gas parameters in predicting these outcomes. A single-center, retrospective, observational study involving 438 hospitalized patients with COVID-19. Associations between imaging findings, clinical severity, comorbidities, and in-hospital death were assessed using Poisson regression, expressed as prevalence ratios (PR) and 95% CIs. The discriminatory performance of inflammatory biomarkers (CRP, LDH, and ferritin) and blood gas parameters (pCO2 and pO2) was analyzed using ROC curves. Computed tomography revealed pulmonary involvement in 92.7% of patients; involvement exceeding 75% was independently associated with greater severity (PR=1.67; 95% CI: 1.27–2.18; p<0.001) and showed a borderline association with in-hospital death (PR=1.47; 95% CI: 0.98–2.21; p=0.05). Chest radiography showed low prognostic value. Obesity was the only comorbidity independently associated with greater pulmonary involvement. Among the biomarkers, LDH showed the best performance for predicting death (AUC=0.77), followed by CRP (AUC=0.67). No marker demonstrated significant discriminatory capacity regarding CT findings.Computed tomography showed greater prognostic value than chest radiography for predicting COVID-19 severity. Obesity was independently associated with greater pulmonary involvement, while LDH was the biomarker with the best discriminatory capacity for in-hospital death. The combined use of CT findings and inflammatory biomarkers may contribute to the prognostic stratification of hospitalized patients.
authors: Aryana Isabelle de Almeida Neves Siqueira
Rozangela Maria de Almeida Fernandes Wyszomirska

title: Korean Temple Food as Plant-Based Food Culture: A Social Big Data Analysis of Changing Online Food Discourse Across the COVID-19 Transition
abstract: This study examines how Korean-language online discourse surrounding Korean temple food evolved across the COVID-19 transition, with particular attention to its changing meanings as a traditional plant-based food culture. A cleaned corpus of 24,353 online documents was analyzed across three three-year periods: pre-COVID-19 (1 January 2017–31 December 2019), COVID-19 (1 January 2020–31 December 2022), and post-endemic (1 June 2023–31 May 2026). Sixty core keywords were selected for each period and examined using frequency analysis, normalized weighted strength (NWS), degree and closeness centrality, semantic network analysis, CONCOR, and Jaccard similarity. Before COVID-19, discourse centered on vegetarianism, cooking, ingredients, dining, and traditional Buddhist food culture. During the pandemic, veganism, nature, health, and healing became more prominent, strengthening associations with plant-based and health-oriented eating. In the post-endemic period, this food identity remained visible while experiential, wellness-related, and media-driven meanings became more distinct. Jaccard similarity was 0.739 for the pre-COVID-19 versus COVID-19 comparison, 0.600 for COVID-19 versus post-endemic, and 0.519 for pre-COVID-19 versus post-endemic, indicating substantial continuity alongside greater compositional differentiation across more temporally distant comparisons and supporting an interpretation of gradual reconfiguration rather than abrupt change. Overall, Korean temple food has been recontextualized as a broader plant-based food culture in which its traditional Buddhist culinary foundations coexist with health, wellness, experiential consumption, and cultural meanings within contemporary online food discourse.

title: HRCT Chest Findings in Moderate to Severe Post Covid-19 Patients at 4 To 8 Weeks Follow Up
abstract: Background and Aims: Though Reverse Transcription Polymerase Chain Reaction (RT-PCR) is the confirmatory diagnostic test of COVID-19 disease, chest Computed Tomography (CT) also plays a crucial role, specially in severity assessment. Some previous studies suggest a risk of fibrotic consequences of COVID-19 disease but little is known yet. The present study aimed to explore the pattern of HRCT chest findings at 4-8 weeks follow-up of the patients recovered from COVID-19. Methods: This cross-sectional study was carried out in the Department of Respiratory Medicine, Dhaka Medical College Hospital. A total of 70 patients were included in this study according to exclusion and inclusion criteria. Informed written consent was taken from each patient. Data collection was done through a pre-structured questionnaire. Collected data were analyzed by using the statistical software SPSS 22. Results: The mean age of the respondents was 52.3 +/- 12.4 (SD) years with a majority in the age group 50-59 years (30%). Clear male predominance was observed (73%). HRCT chest during follow-up at 4 to 8 weeks showed 42.9% partial resolution, 31.4% complete resolution and 25.7% fibrotic changes. In order of frequency, ground-glass opacity (GGO) (65.7%), vascular dilatation (25.7%), consolidation (20%) etc. were the persistent radiological changes at 4 to 8 weeks follow up HRCT chest scan. The presence of hypertension, diabetes mellitus, coronary heart disease, liver disease is significantly associated with fibrotic changes and failure to complete resolution. A more severe initial CT score was associated with persistent radiological changes at follow-up. Conclusion: Extensive study is recommended to validate the findings.

title: Clinical Course and Outcomes of Complicated Community-Acquired Pneumonia in Children During a 5-Year Period Including the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: Objective: Community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) remains a significant cause of morbidity in children. Despite widespread vaccination, the incidence and clinical course of complicated CAP (cCAP) continue to pose diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. This study aimed to evaluate the clinical course, management, and outcomes of children with cCAP in pediatric clinical practice. Methods: This retrospective–prospective observational study was conducted at a tertiary university hospital between December 2019 and December 2024. Children under 18 years of age diagnosed with cCAP were included. Results: A total of 52 children were included, with a median age of 70.5 months; 48.1% were female. Parapneumonic effusion (PPE) was the most common complication (86.5%), followed by empyema (21.2%) and necrotizing pneumonia (7.6%). Bacterial pathogens were identified in a minority of cases. Among the limited number of culture-positive cases, group A Streptococcus and Streptococcus pneumoniae were the most frequently identified organisms (11.5%, n = 6). Chest tube thoracostomy was required in 60% of patients, and surgical intervention in 9.6%. Patients requiring chest tube placement had significantly higher C-reactive protein (CRP) levels and longer durations of intravenous (IV) antibiotic therapy. No mortality was observed. Conclusions: Despite extensive vaccination in healthy children, cases of cCAP still occur, and the causative agent is isolated only in a very few cases. The findings are consistent with the fact that vaccine breakthrough infections, including those caused by pneumococcal serotypes 3 and 14, may still contribute to severe cCAP, whereas group A Streptococcus was identified in a minority of culture-positive cases. Elevated CRP levels at admission may serve as a useful predictor for invasive interventions.

title: Effectiveness of tailored individual follow-up vs. standard one-day group course on health-related quality of life in patients with post COVID-19 condition: a randomized controlled trial
abstract: Background Post COVID-19 condition (PCC), is characterized by a wide range of symptoms, including fatigue and cognitive problems. Symptoms may lead to disability in everyday life and reduced health-related quality of life (HRQoL). Evidence for effective rehabilitation strategies for this patient group remains limited. Objective To examine the effectiveness of tailored individual follow-up compared with a standard one-day group course, both based on cognitive behavioral approach, in patients with PCC 6 months after the intervention. Methods A single-center, parallel-group, superiority randomized controlled trial (1:1) was conducted among outpatients aged 18–65 years with PCC. Patients were randomized to either a rehabilitation program with individual follow-up over 6–8 weeks or a standard one-day multidisciplinary self-management group course. Both groups were introduced to graded activity based on principles from cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) and were offered the app “My COVID rehabilitation”. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in patient reported HRQoL (EQ-5D-5L-index score) at 6 months. Secondary self-reported outcomes included fatigue measured with the Chalder Fatigue Scale, EQ-VAS, and symptom registration. Neuropsychological function was assessed with objective neuropsychological tests. Results 60 participants were randomized, the mean age was 46 years (22–66 years), and 43 (72%) were female. Outcome assessments were completed for the primary outcome for 29 participants in each arm. No significant between-group difference was found in the primary outcome (score difference EQ-5D-5L-index =0.07; 95% CI [-0.18,.04]; p = .11). The adjusted linear model confirmed the absence of significant difference between groups. No persistent significant group differences were observed for any secondary outcomes. Both groups showed statistically and clinically significant sustained improvements in fatigue and EQ-VAS, as well as significant reductions in the number of symptoms. Within neuropsychological test, both groups demonstrated significant improvement in episodic memory (RAVLT), and the standard course group additionally showed significant improvement in attention (CPT). Conclusion Tailored individual follow-up was not more effective than a standard one-day group course in improving HRQoL in PCC, both based on principles of CBT. However, significant improvements in both groups were observed in several secondary outcomes, including some objective neuropsychological tests. Larger studies are needed to confirm these results. Clinical Trial Registration : https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06085911 , identifier NCT06085911.

title: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of COVID-19 Cases in 75 Countries Using Google Trends: A Retrospective Study
abstract: Few studies have systematically examined the predictive capacity of digital search data for forecasting COVID-19 cases on a global scale, particularly in terms of search queries in different languages. Additionally, limited research has explored the correlations and temporal dynamics between digital search data in different languages and clinical cases. Therefore, this study employed Google Trends using COVID-19-related search terms in English and local languages to predict World Health Organization reported cases across 75 countries, spanning Africa, the Americas, Asia and Oceania, and Europe. Correlations between Google Trends and clinical case data were evaluated, and time-lagged cross-correlation analysis was employed to estimate the temporal dynamics of search data relative to cases. We also developed a machine learning-based random forest model to predict clinical cases using combined English and local language Google Trends. Our results identified leading time lags in most countries, suggesting that Google Trends can provide early warnings of reported clinical case surges. Furthermore, our random forest model successfully predicted COVID-19 cases using combined English and local language search data in a retrospective analysis, with identified relative contributions of English versus local-language searches. This study demonstrates that digital search data provide an openly accessible source of information that may assist forecasting of infectious disease outbreak surges prior to clinical data reporting. Digital epidemiology-based approaches could support public health decision-making by potentially complementing existing clinical and wastewater surveillance systems for infectious diseases. This work directly contributes to the United Nations sustainable development goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-Being) and SDG 11 (Sustainable and Resilient Cities and Communities).

title: A Cross-Sectional Survey on Proportion of Post COVID-19 Health Problems among Health Care Workers in a Tertiary Care Hospital in Thiruvanthapuram District
abstract: COVID-19 is an infectious disease caused by recently discovered coronavirus. This new virus and disease were unknown before the outbreak began in -*Wuhan, China, in December 2019.Post-coronavirus disease syndrome includes persistence of symptoms beyond viral clearance and fresh development of symptoms or exaggeration of chronic diseases within a month after initial clinical and virological cure of the disease with a viral aetiology. The present study was aimed to identify the proportion of post covid 19 health problems among health care workers in a tertiary care hospital in Thiruvananthapuram. The objectives of the study were to identify the proportion of post covid 19 health problems among health care workers and find out the factors associated with post covid 19 health related problems and selected socio personal and clinical variables Methodology: The researcher adopted quantitative research approach. Purposive sampling technique was used to collect data from a total of 70 samples Data was collected using Structured questionnaire and Depression Anxiety Stress scale. Results: Based on the socio personal and clinical variables 51.5% of health care workers were below 30years of age and 84.3% were female health care workers. Majority of (47.1%) health care workers were graduates. Based on thecomorbidities75.1% of the health care workers had no comorbidities and 11.4% have thyroid disorders. Majority of healthcare workers (95.7) % had no ill habits. Only 4.3% were alcoholic and 71.4% of health care workers had no habit of doing physical exercise. 72.5% of health care workers had fever during acute covid 19 infection period. 38.57% of health care workers had shortness of breath as respiratory problems in the post covid 19 period. Based on the cardiovascular problems in the post covid 19 period, 21.43% of health care workers had extreme shortness of breath with exertion. 8.57% of health care workers had diarrhoea and 2.9% of health care workers had frequent urination and oedema in the post covid 19 period. 22.85% of health care workers had headache.47.14% had fatigue in the post covid 19 period. Based on the psychological problems 15.7% of health care workers had mild stress 8.6% of health care workers had severe anxiety and majority of subjects (81.4%) had no depression. In the post covid 19 physical problems, there was statistically significant association between working hours (chi-square value= 0.011, p p<0.05) with fatigue, marital status with extreme shortness of breath with exertion (chi-square value= 0.005, p<0.05), type of family with diarrhoea (chi-square value= 0.016, p<0.05), gender with headache (chi-square value= 0.041, p<0.05) and educational status (chi-square value= 0.001, p<0.05). Gender with hair loss (chi-square value= 0.002, p<0.05) and gender with marital status (chi-square value= 0.008, p<0.05). In post covid 19 psychological problems there was statistically significant association between working days with depression (chi-square value 0.050, p<0.05), educational status with anxiety (chi-square value= 0.045, p<0.05). There was statistically no significant association between post covid 19 physical problems with socio personal variables and clinical variables. The study findings concluded that post covid 19 health problems like fatigue and hair loss as physical problems and stress and anxiety as psychological problems among health care workers.

title: Effectiveness of deep recurrent neural networks in classifying COVID-19-related respiratory conditions using clinical reports
abstract: Abstract Countries all around the world have been severely affected by the novel coronavirus, popularly known as COVID-19, causing hundreds of thousands of unfortunate deaths without having found a widespread immunization method. It is extremely crucial for healthcare officials and the Governments of various countries to be able to differentiate the possible coronavirus strains to provide appropriate care and treatment. This paper proposes an effective way to set apart coronavirus strains into classes such as severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS), acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), and COVID-19 using machine learning algorithms and recurrent neural networks (RNN). Natural language processing (NLP) techniques were performed on textual clinical reports to structure the data and improve its usability for the model. Bag of words model and Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency (TF-IDF) vectorization were some of the few processes involved in extracting the prominent symptoms associated with each variant. The same has fed to various machine learning algorithms include multinomial naive Bayes (NB), logistic regression (LR), decision tree (DT), support vector machines (SVMs), and random forest (RF). Moreover, two more algorithms namely bagging, and gradient boost, are used for classification purposes. The reasons for choosing them are to observe their performance while classifying the proposed problem and compare the overall potency of the prediction system with RNNs. From this investigation, RNNs proved to be the optimal and expeditious technique to distinguish the covid strains. Adding more layers to the RNN has been noted to increase the efficacy of the system. The proposed approach with RNNs is giving an accuracy of around 99.14%.

title: Cryptogenic organizing pneumonia vs. covid-19
abstract: Cryptogenic organizing pneumonia (COP) is a rare entity characterized by connective tissue and fibrosis inside the bronchioles. The clinical presentation is non-specific and begins with a dry cough, shortness of breath, fever, myalgias, and weight loss. Diagnosis is based on clinical history, objective examination, analyses, spirometry, and imaging tests (high-resolution computed tomography, fibrobroncoschopy, and bronchoalveolar lavage). Lung biopsy is the gold-standard diagnostic test, but it should only be carried out if necessary to establish a differential diagnosis. According to the literature, glucocorticoids are effective with immunomodulators (macrolides) or chemotherapy agentes depending on the underlying pathology. The following case refers to a patient with a respiratory infection, in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic, and who, despite their clinical similarities, was diagnosed with COP. It is important to emphasize the importance of making a differential diagnosis, which will allow an appropriate therapeutic plan to be drawn up.

title: Patients' and Psychotherapists' Evaluation of Remote Psychotherapy During the COVID ‐19 Pandemic: What Can We Learn for Future Extraordinary Circumstances and Public Health Emergencies?
abstract: During the COVID‐19 pandemic, psychotherapists and patients experienced a rapid, unplanned transition from face‐to‐face to remote therapy. Understanding their experiences with this transition may help inform the implementation of remote psychotherapy during future extraordinary circumstances and public health emergencies. We aimed to investigate patients' and therapists' expectations, therapeutic relationship and overall satisfaction with remote therapy compared to face‐to‐face therapy during the first wave of the COVID‐19 pandemic. Eighty‐three patients and 32 psychotherapists at a university cognitive behavioural therapy outpatient clinic filled out a handwritten survey, including Likert scales and open questions regarding the aspects listed above. Overall, patients had optimistic expectations, appraised the therapeutic relationship positively and were mostly ‘very satisfied’ with remote therapy, regardless of whether they received telephone or video therapy ( p s ≥ 0.121). Therapists were more critical in terms of expectations, satisfaction and their appraisal of the therapeutic relationship, especially for telephone compared to video therapy ( p s ≤ 0.015). Remote psychotherapy offers a viable substitution to face‐to‐face therapy in the context of extraordinary circumstances and public health emergencies. Patients were overall satisfied with remote therapy forms and felt like they were in good hands with their therapists. The more critical appraisal from therapists highlights the need for adapted intervention techniques and specific training for delivering remote therapy.

title: COVID-19 E NEUROPATIAS AUTOIMUNES: UMA ANÁLISE DA RELAÇÃO COM A SÍNDROME DE GUILLAIN-BARRÉ COVID-19 AND AUTOIMMUNE NEUROPATHIES: AN ANALYSIS OF THE RELATIONSHIP WITH GUILLAIN-BARRÉ SYNDROME COVID-19 Y NEUROPATÍAS AUTOINMUNES: UN ANÁLISIS DE LA RELACIÓN CON EL SÍNDROME DE GUILLAIN-BARRÉ
abstract: Esse artigo buscou compreender e analisar a fisiopatologia da SGB e investigar a relação entre a doença e a infecção pelo SARS-CoV-2. Realizou-se uma revisão sistemática da literatura por meio de uma pesquisa nas bases de dados PubMed, LILACS e CAPES. Foram aplicados critérios de inclusão e exclusão, culminando na seleção de 24 estudos relevantes para embasar este trabalho. As análises evidenciaram uma associação consistente entre a SGB e a COVID-19, refletida no aumento de casos durante a pandemia. A infecção pelo SARS-CoV-2 é capaz de desencadear uma resposta imunológica anormal, contribuindo para o desenvolvimento da SGB em pacientes infectados pelo vírus. Apesar da associação evidente entre a COVID-19 e a SGB, os mecanismos imunológicos subjacentes a essa relação ainda não estão completamente elucidados. Estudos futuros são imprescindíveis para aprofundar o conhecimento sobre os subtipos da doença, refinar o diagnóstico e aprimorar as estratégias terapêuticas e de manejo clínico.

title: Cross talk between SARS-CoV-2 and the angiotensin system: clinical implications
abstract: This study characterizes the interaction between the angiotensin system and angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2)/spike proteins and its significance for coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) severity. Using a cell-to-cell fusion assay and angiotensin 1 receptor (AT1R) activation assessment via the AT1R-Tango approach, we reveal a crucial role of ACE2 in attenuating AT1R activation. Furthermore, the data indicate that the spike protein indirectly amplifies AT1R activation. In addition, angiotensin 1–7 (Ang 1–7) was identified to act not only as Mas receptor (MasR) agonist, but also as a biased agonist for AT1R.

title: Assessing the Efficacy and Challenges of Tofacitinib in the Management of COVID-19: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Cohort Studies
abstract: Objectives: Global healthcare faces challenges in combating COVID-19, with rising cases despite widespread vaccination. Severe COVID-19 cases, marked by acute respiratory distress and cytokine release syndrome, highlight the importance of managing cytokine storms. Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitors, such as tofacitinib, show promise in this regard. While tofacitinib is recommended for severe cases, challenges include adverse effects, conflicting studies, and the need for further investigation of new virus strains. Overcoming these hurdles is crucial for developing an effective treatment protocol and reducing COVID-19 mortality. Methods: This study conducted a comprehensive search across PubMed, Scopus, and ISI Web of Science for observational studies on tofacitinib treatment in human adults with COVID-19. The search covered a specified period up to 2024. Data extraction, including study characteristics and quality assessment, employed the Newcastle Ottawa Scale and a modified Cochrane tool. Statistical analysis, conducted with Comprehensive Meta-Analysis Software, assessed heterogeneity and significance levels. Results: The meta-analysis of the three studies showed a significant reduction in mortality (Risk Ratio: 0.372, 95% CI: 0.213–0.649, P-value = 0.001) with low heterogeneity (Cochrane P-value = 0.793), while no significant reduction in the need for mechanical ventilation was observed (Cochrane P-value = 0.194). Conclusion: Tofacitinib administration shows a significant reduction in COVID-19 mortality. However, the limited studies on its efficacy highlight the need for cautious interpretation in clinical assessments.

title: The Post-COVID-19 Study Experience: Modes of Study, Technology Use, and Socialisation at the University of Latvia
abstract: This study explores how the post-COVID-19 era has affected higher education at the University of Latvia, examining perceived changes in teaching and learning, the study process, and socialisation, and comparing student and teacher perspectives. A quantitative online survey used a structured QuestionPro questionnaire; this paper analyses six questions on post-COVID-19 experiences in higher education. Altogether 1,053 responses were analysed (970 students; 83 teachers), using descriptive statistics and inferential tests (Mann–Whitney U) with effect sizes to assess group differences. The findings indicate positive changes in higher education following the pandemic, particularly greater flexibility in the study process, the provision of different modes of study, increased opportunities for online learning, and broader use of digital technologies. The post-COVID-19 period also appears to have contributed to the development of digital competence among both teachers and students, suggesting progress in addressing the digital gap that existed before the pandemic. However, personalised and student-centred pedagogies remain only partly implemented, and some tendencies towards returning to traditional forms of higher education were identified. COVID-19 has brought inevitable and lasting changes to higher education. While some practices appear to be reverting to pre-pandemic models, students’ positive attitudes towards greater flexibility and digital opportunities may support the development of a more inclusive and sustainable higher education. Research restrictions. Limitations include restricted generalisability, as the study examines a single case; broader and longitudinal follow-up research is recommended. Questions on internet accessibility were not included.

title: Effects of COVID-19 pandemic on physical activity in children and young adults with implanted devices.
abstract: Children and young adults with preexisting cardiovascular disease (CVD) may be disproportionately affected by the collateral health consequences of the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic. In addition to a higher risk of morbidity and mortality from COVID-19, young persons with CVD may be more susceptible to alterations in physical activity (PA) and poor health outcomes owing to the unprecedented loss of structured school days, reduced sports participation, increased screen time, and social isolation. However, data on the acute and long-term effects of the pandemic on PA in young persons with established CVD risk remain scarce.

title: Strengthening patient safety through biosafety and infection prevention measures during COVID-19: a policy and practice review
abstract: The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) placed substantial pressure on global healthcare systems, biosafety management, and the delivery of safe clinical services. As a critical component of infection prevention and control (IPC), biosafety contributes not only to limiting pathogen exposure but also to protecting healthcare workers, maintaining reliable diagnostic pathways, and supporting patient safety and health-service continuity. This Policy and Practice Review presents a structured narrative synthesis of a sample of literature published primarily between January 2020 and August 2026, supplemented by selected earlier foundational studies and relevant public-health guidance. The review focuses on respiratory exposure control, appropriate use and oversight of personal protective equipment (PPE), airway-management safety, emergency respirator decontamination and reuse strategies including ultraviolet germicidal irradiation (UVGI), specimen collection and transport, laboratory biosafety, and emerging diagnostic technologies. The evidence indicates that safe practice requires layered, risk-based measures adapted to the exposure context and specific clinical or laboratory activity. During severe PPE shortages, UVGI was investigated as a contingency strategy for respirator decontamination, but microbial inactivation, preservation of filtration performance, and maintenance of fit or seal integrity represent distinct outcomes and require separate validation. Safe specimen pathways similarly depend on validated collection, transport, storage, and laboratory procedures that preserve both worker safety and diagnostic reliability. Emerging CRISPR- and nanomaterial-enabled technologies may improve diagnostic accessibility or turnaround time, but their contribution to patient safety depends on clinical validation, quality assurance, regulatory oversight, and successful integration into healthcare workflows. Overall, lessons from the COVID-19 pandemic support a multilayered, activity-specific approach to biosafety that integrates occupational protection, diagnostic safety, patient safety, and health-system resilience.

title: Five Years After the Onset of the COVID-19 Pandemic: Changing Epidemiology of SARS-CoV-2 and Seasonal Respiratory Viruses in Hospitalized Adults
abstract: Pandemic non-pharmaceutical interventions disrupted seasonal respiratory virus circulation, but longer-term pathogen-specific patterns in hospitalized adults remain incompletely defined. We evaluated detections across three nonconsecutive respiratory seasons from early relaxation of pandemic measures to five years after pandemic onset. This retrospective, observational, single-center cohort study included 2249 adults hospitalized with pneumonia, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease exacerbation, or asthma exacerbation who underwent multiplex polymerase chain reaction testing in September 2021–May 2022, September 2022–May 2023, or September 2025–May 2026. Influenza A positivity peaked in the second period (12.6%) and decreased to 6.8% in the third (p < 0.001). SARS-CoV-2 likewise peaked in the second period (9.2%) and declined to 1.5% in the third (p < 0.001). Respiratory syncytial virus increased from 0.5% in the first period to 4.9% and 3.8% in the second and third periods, respectively (p < 0.001). Positivity for other respiratory viruses did not differ (16.0%, 16.9%, and 19.1%; p = 0.308). Viral co-detection was highest in the second period (6.1% vs. 2.6% and 2.8%; p < 0.001). Respiratory virus epidemiology remained dynamic five years after pandemic onset, supporting sustained multi-pathogen surveillance.

title: Criteria for Distinguishing Pulmonary Tuberculosis from Community-Acquired Pneumonia of Moderate to Severe Course and Associated with COVID-19. Part 2
abstract: The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, particularly during its early stages, was characterised by the rapid spread of SARS-CoV-2 infection, which triggered activation of the immune system followed by its subsequent exhaustion. As a result, immune control over Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB) was impaired, especially in regions with a high tuberculosis burden and a significant prevalence of latent tuberculosis (TB) infection. These changes may have contributed to a more severe course of tuberculosis and potentially increa­sed the risk of developing resistance to anti-tuberculosis drugs. Objective — to evaluate the relationship between the clinical severity, the cell-mediated immune response, endogenous intoxication, and nitro-oxidative stress in patients with pulmonary tuberculosis, infected with different strains of MTB and concomitant SARS-CoV-2. Materials and methods. A prospective study included 191 newly diagnosed patients with pulmonary TB, distributed into four groups: the 1st study group (1st SG) included 80 patients with drug-susceptible TB, the 2nd study group (2nd SG) comprised 40 patients with primary multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB), the 3rd study group (3rd SG) consisted of 49 patients with acquired MDR-TB, and the 4th study group (4th SG) included 22 patients (11 with drug-susceptible TB and 11 with primary MDR-TB) co-infected with SARS-CoV-2. The indices were compared with those of a control group (CG) of 36 conventionally healthy individuals. The laboratory investigations included immunophenotyping of CD3+, CD4+, CD8+, and CD19+ cells, C-reactive protein, ceruloplasmin, circulating immune complexes (CICs), tumour necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), interleu­kin-6 (IL-6) and interleukin-8 (IL-8), leukocyte and hematologic intoxication indices, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR). Clinical-radiological findings indicated a more severe TB evolution in patients with acquired MDR-TB and those co-infected with SARS-CoV-2, supported by depletion of CD3+, CD4+, CD8+ and CD16+ cells, and strong negative correlations between immune cell levels and disease severity. Acquired MDR-TB and SARS-CoV-2 co-infection determine severe clinical-radiological evolution, pronounced cell-mediated immune depletion, sustained immune complex formation and acute-phase activation, intensified cytokine-driven inflammation and nitro-oxidative stress, overall contributing to enhanced immune dysregulation.

title: Neuropsychiatric Manifestations and Their Impact in Post-COVID-19 Condition: A Study in A Tertiary Care Center in Bangladesh
abstract: Background: Post-COVID conditions are a wide range of new, returning, or ongoing symptoms a person can experience four or more weeks after first suffering from COVID-19. Quantification of these conditions and their impact on the patient’s daily living was scarce in the current literature. This study aimed to observe the different neuropsychiatric conditions in the post-COVID conditions with their severity. Additionally, we evaluated their impact on the patient’s life. Methods: This was a cross-sectional study. We followed up with the patients attending the COVID-19 post-COVID clinic of Dhaka Medical College. The study was conducted at the COVID- 19 post-acute care and follow-up clinic unit of Dhaka Medical College Hospital from January 01, 2021 to June 15, 2022. Results: In this cross-sectional study, we included 400 patients with post-COVID conditions. The mean age (SD) of the study population was 44.8 (15.5); most were male (51%), and most patients (203, 50.8%) had mild Illness. The most prominent post-COVID-19 Neuropsychiatric features were fatigue (283, 70.8%), Headache (104, 26%), memory disturbances (107, 26.8%), and depression (109,27.8%). Most patients did not fully recover; the functional scores with Karnofsky’s rating were 89.8 (7.2). Most patients reported more than usual tiredness (127, 41.1%), needed to rest more (116, 37.5%), and felt weak (183, 59.2%). About 30% of patients had Headache, mostly throbbing (69, 56.5%), bilateral, and mild in severity. Increasing age (OR, 95%CI, p-value, 1.03, 1.01-1.05, 0.002) and moderate severity COVID-19 (OR, 95%CI, p-value, 7.3, 2.3-39.05, 0.02) were the risk factors for fatigue. Increasing age was the risk factor for Headaches. Conclusions: In the post-COVID conditions, a significant number of patient had been suffering from various neuropsychiatric conditions and were not able to return to their previous functional status.

title: From the COVID‐19 Pandemic to Crises: Lessons for Canadian Climate Governance
abstract: Abstract The COVID‐19 pandemic was the most significant governance stress test in recent Canadian history, revealing both the capacities and constraints of Canadian public administration under acute uncertainty. This article examines Canada's pandemic response as a diagnostic case for understanding governance capacity relevant to long‐duration challenges such as climate change. Drawing on interviews with senior public health and climate‐health leaders, and triangulating these insights with federal evaluations, the analysis focuses on coordination, trust, political will, and institutional learning across pandemic phases. Findings show that coordination and political will were episodic rather than durably embedded, trust was a fragile governance resource, and post‐crisis learning was only weakly institutionalized. Rather than treating COVID‐19 as a model for climate governance, the article argues that its value lies in diagnosis: making visible the limits of emergency‐oriented governance and clarifying the capacities required for more anticipatory, durable responses.

title: Features of the dental status in COVID-19 patients
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic, caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, has significantly affected medical practice, presenting new challenges in the fields of diagnosis, treatment, and preventive measures. Objective — to analyze changes in dental status among individuals following COVID-19, taking into account the presence of xerostomia symptoms and signs of inflammatory periodontal diseases. Materials and methods. The dental status of 454 patients who were hospitalized for COVID-19 treatment between 2021 and 2024 was assessed. Depending on the severity of the disease, the patients were divided into two groups: Group I consisted of patients with severe COVID-19 (n=225; main group), while Group II included patients with moderate COVID-19 (n=229; comparison group). Dental status was assessed according to WHO recommendations using the DMFT, PMA, and PBI indices. The clinical manifestations of COVID-19 were associated with a high prevalence (76.8—100%) of oral manifestations, including dysgeusia, dry mouth, and vesiculobullous lesions of the oral mucosa. Patients with severe COVID-19 were significantly more likely to experience taste disturbances (93.3%) and olfactory disturbances (97.8%), oral mucosal lesions (97.8%), oral pain (97.8%), dry mouth (100%), and pronounced tongue coating (87.6%; p<0.001). At the same time, halitosis and gingival bleeding occurred with equal frequency (100%) in both groups. Assessment of dental indices revealed unsatisfactory oral hygiene (OHI-S=3.3–4.3) and a high prevalence of dental caries among all examined patients. However, patients in Group I demonstrated more pronounced signs of periodontal tissue inflammation, as indicated by higher PMA (85.6–92.2%) and PBI (2.1–3.7) index scores. Periodontitis and cheilitis were diagnosed in all patients, whereas oral candidiasis (52% of patients) and aphthous stomatitis (72.9%) were significantly more common in patients with severe COVID-19 (p<0.05). COVID-19 has a negative impact on oral health, particularly in patients with severe disease. The findings highlight the need for timely dental examinations, preventive measures, and comprehensive follow-up of patients after recovering from the infection.

title: Post-pandemic mortality patterns and COVID-19 burden considering multiple death causes
abstract: Post-pandemic mortality rates can explore the residual COVID-19 burden and changes in other causes of death. Considering weighted multiple causes of death from death certificates (underlying and others) may help compare post- versus pre-pandemic mortality patterns, while potentially reducing the impact of cause misattribution. Estimates of post-pandemic impact are critical also for proper continuing public health policies (e.g. We retrospectively analyse national all-cause mortality rate ratios between 2024 and pre-pandemic years (2017-2019) for sex-stratified 10-year age groups in Austria. In weighted analyses, the underlying death cause was weighted 50% and other causes shared the remaining 50%. Sensitivity analyses explored different weightings. Cause-specific weightings were also compared between 2024 and 2019. Despite 1212 reported COVID-19 deaths in 2024, all-cause mortality rates were equal or lower in 2024 compared to 2019 in all strata at risk from COVID-19 (i.e., aged 60 years and over). All-cause mortality rates in 2024 were higher than in 2019 in adolescent and young adult strata. The ratio of weighted over unweighted COVID-19 death rates was 0.51-0.58 for age strata 60 years and older and even lower in sensitivity analyses, indicating that COVID-19 deaths were possibly overestimated. Post-pandemic COVID-19 deaths had no visible impact on mortality patterns in Austria and were possibly overcounted. Increased post-pandemic mortality patterns in the young are particularly worrisome.

title: Unveiling structural determinants of peptide recognition by public and private SARS-CoV-2-specific T-cell receptors
abstract: Abstract Public T cell receptors (TCRs) recurrently emerge across individuals in response to common pathogens, yet the structural and biophysical basis distinguishing public from private clonotypes remains incompletely defined. Here, we combine epitope mapping, single-cell TCR sequencing, and single-particle cryo-electron microscopy to dissect CD8 + T cell responses to the immunodominant SARS-CoV-2 ORF3a (207-215) epitope presented by HLA-A*01:01. Among responding clonotypes, we identify a public TCR (TCR pub ), shared across donors, and a private TCR (TCR priv ) that uses nearly identical β chains but distinct α chains. Despite comparable micromolar affinities and functional avidities, cryo-EM structures at ~3 Å resolution reveal that the two receptors engage the peptide-MHC complex through distinct CDR-loop configurations and contact footprints. TCR pub establishes contacts with the peptide and the MHC α2-helix primarily through the CDR2β and CDR3β loops, whereas TCR priv distributes contacts across both MHC α-helices and engages the peptide via multiple CDR loops. In agreement with these observations, alanine-scanning mutagenesis reveals that TCR pub shows greater sensitivity to peptide substitutions, consistent with its peptide-focused binding mode. These findings demonstrate how alternative α-chain pairing reconfigures the antigen-binding interface within a shared β-chain.

title: Non-fluorescent benzothiadiazole probe with protein-triggered turn-on fluorescence for imaging SARS-CoV-2 spike protein in biological systems
abstract: Herein, we report a non-fluorescent 2,1,3-benzothiadiazole (BTD) derivative, BTD-PhCOOH, as a protein-triggered fluorogenic platform for SARS-CoV-2 spike protein detection. Direct coupling under mild refrigerated conditions afforded the BTD-Spike conjugate, producing an intense green fluorescence signal and demonstrating efficient fluorescence turn-on after protein ligation. Solvent-accessible surface area analysis (SASA) identified Lys529 as the most accessible lysine residue, providing a structural rationale for conjugate formation. In MCF-7 cells, BTD-Spike enabled time-dependent visualization of spike-associated cellular interactions, with membrane-associated fluorescence after 30 min and a more defined peripheral and intracellular punctate pattern after 60 min. In mice, systemic intravenous administration established the current sensitivity limits of visible-range whole-body and ex vivo organ fluorescence imaging, as treated animals could not be clearly distinguished from controls under these acquisition conditions. Importantly, higher-resolution confocal analysis of fixed brain tissue revealed localized fluorescence differences between treated and control samples. Additionally, direct intracerebroventricular administration enabled brain-level detection of both BTD-Spike and BTD-labeled amyloid-β, generating qualitatively distinct fluorescence patterns in the central nervous system. Overall, BTD-PhCOOH establishes a protein-activated fluorescence platform strongly supported by chemical, photophysical, computational, and cellular validation, while the brain-detection experiments highlight its potential for probing protein-associated signals in complex biological environments.

title: A socio-onomastic investigation of Covid-19 in selected Yoruba-speaking communities, Osun State, Nigeria
abstract: This study investigated the cultural and social aspects of names and naming practices (socio-onomastics) associated with Covid-19 in selected Yoruba-speaking communities in Osun State Nigeria, using the mixed design – a blend of the qualitative and quantitative research traditions. Seven hundred (700) respondents (35 randomly selected from each of 20 selected rural communities in Oriade Local Government Area Osun State of Nigeria) were the subjects of the investigation. Additional primary data for the study were sourced from a content analysis of Alaroye, a leading Yoruba newspaper. Results reveal that the communities use 24 dominant names and expressions under 11 distinct categories for Covid-19. Historical referent, coinage, and containment protocols produced more names than other sources of socio-onomastics frame. Inconclusive findings were found regarding the influences of media on the socio-onomastic process. A very unique result of the investigation was the reinforcement of socio-linguistic theory that people invent words and expressions based on historical influences; comparison to similar phenomena; personal experiences, borrowed names and terms and shared experiences to interpret new phenomena such as health emergencies. The authors recommend that health agencies should incorporate socio-onomastics praxis and conduct more studies on the Tricyle/OSMR Communication Model, to facilitate communication towards attaining good health and well-being in rural areas of Southwest Nigeria, especially during health emergencies.

title: Association of IFN ‐γ +874 T/A Polymorphism With COVID ‐19 Susceptibility, Severity, and Inflammatory Response: A Case–Control Study From Southern Iran
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Significant interpatient variability in Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID‐19) manifestations highlights the influence of host genetic factors on disease outcomes. This study examines its association with COVID‐19 susceptibility, severity, and inflammatory markers in an Iranian population. Methods A retrospective case–control analysis was performed on 210 COVID‐19 patients and 210 age‐ and sex‐matched control subjects to evaluate whether the Interferon‐gamma (IFN‐γ) gene polymorphism (+874 T/A) is associated with disease severity. Results Patients had more comorbidities (e.g., diabetes 26.2% vs. 14.3%; hypertension 29.5% vs. 16.7%) and pronounced paraclinical abnormalities, including elevated Neutrophil‐to‐Lymphocyte Ratio (NLR) (8.1 vs. 1.9), C‐reactive protein (CRP) (45.5 vs. 3.2 mg/L), and lymphopenia (1.1 vs. 2.1 × 10 3 /μL; all p < 0.001). The TA genotype and A allele increased disease susceptibility (Odds Ratio (OR) =2.05 (95% CI: 1.32–3.19), p = 0.002; OR = 1.58 (95% CI: 1.11–2.25), p = 0.01, respectively). The TA genotype independently predicted severe disease (aOR = 2.85, p = 0.001), and both the TA and AA genotypes were linked to higher IL‐6 levels ( p < 0.001). TT carriers had shorter hospitalizations ( p < 0.01). Combining TA/AA with NLR improved severity prediction (AUC = 0.82 (95% CI: 0.76–0.88)). Conclusion The IFN‐γ +874 TA genotype was independently associated with severe COVID‐19. The TA genotype appears to confer increased risk of severe disease, whereas the AA genotype may be linked to a milder clinical presentation despite elevated inflammatory markers. Integration of genetic and hematological parameters may enhance risk stratification; however, further validation in larger and diverse populations is warranted.

title: Infantile COVID-19: An Evidence-based and Updated Narrative Review
abstract: Infantile COVID-19, caused by SARS-CoV-2, presents unique challenges in diagnosis, management, and outcomes compared to adults. Due to their physiological limits, infants, defined as children under one year old, are categorized among vulnerable health groups, highlighting the importance of effective and timely prevention, diagnosis, and treatment. This review provides the latest evidence on the epidemiology, prevention, clinical diagnosis, and treatment of COVID-19 infection in infants, discussing the existing controversies and highlighting current knowledge gaps. An extensive literature search was performed in MEDLINE (via PubMed), Web of Science, and Scopus databases with relevant free keywords and MeSH terms to identify related records without any restrictions in time or language. Generally exhibiting nonspecific symptoms, COVID-19 can overlap with common respiratory infections among infants. Moreover, the lack of effective verbal communication in infants complicates the symptom assessment, turning the timely diagnosis into a difficult challenge for healthcare providers. Additionally, maternal transmission of SARS-CoV-2 during pregnancy, childbirth, or postpartum care also raises concerns about neonatal infection, with potential implications for both maternal and infant health. Several agents have been proposed for the treatment of infantile COVID-19, including glucocorticoids, intravenous immunoglobulin, tocilizumab, and antivirals such as remdesivir, ritonavir, and favipiravir. Current evidence supports the potential effectiveness of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation and nutrition supplements; however, their ultimate effectiveness is still controversial. As an effective preventive strategy, more studies are required to determine the safety and efficacy of vaccination in this population. The complexity of diagnostic and clinical management associated with COVID-19 poses serious challenges for this group of patients. In managing infantile COVID-19, supportive care is still critical, emphasizing good nutritional support, efficient oxygenation, and hemodynamic maintenance. Given the limited available evidence on immunomodulators, antiviral medications, and other pharmaceutical interventions in this population, safety and efficacy profiles must be carefully considered. Future research should focus on the effectiveness of vaccination, the safety of the currently proposed treatments, and the long-term consequences of COVID-19 infection.

title: Evaluation of the Effect of Vaccination Status on Lung Involvement and Hospitalization in COVID-19 Patients
abstract: Background: The spectrum of COVID-19 in adults ranges from asymptomatic infection to mild respiratory tract symptoms to severe pneumonia with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and multiorgan dysfunction. In our study, it was aimed to investigate the effects of COVID- 19 vaccine on lung involvement and hospitalization. Materials and Methods: Cases over the age of 18, who had a history of contact with cases infected with COVID-19 or had clinical findings suggestive of COVID-19, who applied to the emergency department and who were diagnosed with COVID-19 by reverse-transcriptase-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) were included in the study. Age, gender, comorbid diseases, hospitalization status, thorax tomography findings, and vaccination status in the last 3 months of the patients included in the study were obtained by examining the hospital information system and patient files. Results: Our study included 496 patients. One hundred eighty-three of the cases were vaccinated and 42.6% (n = 78) of the vaccinated patients were male. Of the 313 unvaccinated patients, 36% (n = 113) were male. Comorbid disease was observed in 55.2% (n = 101) of the vaccinated patients and 38.7% (n = 121) of the unvaccinated patients. Of the 313 unvaccinated patients, 72.2% (n = 226) were discharged from the emergency department, 19.8% (n = 62) were admitted to the service, and 8% (n = 25) were admitted to the intensive care unit. Of the 183 vaccinated patients, 78.1% (n = 143) were discharged from the emergency department, 16.4% (n = 30) were admitted to the service, and 5.5% (n = 10) were admitted to the intensive care unit. In the vaccinated patient group, both the service admission rate and the intensive care hospitalization rate were found to be significantly lower than the non-vaccinated patient group (p Conclusion: In our study, it was found that vaccination significantly reduced hospitalization in COVID-19 patients. Although the mean age was higher in the vaccinated patient group, both the service admission rate and the intensive care admission rate were found to be lower.

title: Correlation between Soluble Immunosenescence Biomarkers and Serum Neopterin Levels after COVID-19 Vaccination in a Geriatric Population
abstract: The geriatric population is increasing worldwide, including in Indonesia which has reached 11.01% in 2021 as the leading country in the geriatric population in Southeast Asia. Consequently, there is an increased risk of having severe infection, malignancy, and autoimmunity. Aging of immunity (immunosenescence) is responsible not only for those conditions but also affects the immune response to vaccination. The study's purpose was to analyze the correlation between immunosenescence and a decreased cellular immune response between 6 and 24 weeks after the second dose of CoronaVac vaccination in the geriatric population. This was an observational analytical study with a prospective cohort design. 73 geriatric subjects (≥ 60 years old) who had already received a second dose of CoronaVac were included. All the subjects had blood taken at 6 and 24 weeks after the second dose of CoronaVac. Serum sCD28, sCD80, and sCTLA-4 were used as immunosenescence markers. The decrease in cellular immunity was measured by the decreasing level of serum neopterin between 6 and 24 weeks following vaccine administration. There is a moderate correlation between sCD28, sCD80, and sCTLA-4 with serum neopterin at weeks 6 and 24. We also found a significant correlation between the decrease in neopterin at 6 and 24 weeks with sCD80 (p = 0.016, r = 0.282) but not with sCD28 (p = 0.078, r = 0.207) or sCTLA-4 (p = 0.017, r = 0.279). sCD80 and sCTLA-4 correlated with a more rapid decrease in neopterin level after CoronaVac vaccination in the geriatric population.

title: Luminal pH Regulation of SARS-CoV-2 Trafficking
abstract: This research, conducted in the University of Michigan Dearborn Biophysics Lab, examines how endosomal acidity influences the movement of SARS CoV 2 particles inside human cardiomyocyte like cells. After entering a cell, the virus travels through small compartments called endosomes, which become more acidic as they mature. This acidification helps process the viral Spike protein and release the viral genome, but the role of early endosomal pH in intracellular transport remains unclear. To study this process, NHE9, an endosomal sodium proton exchanger that makes endosomes less acidic, was overexpressed in AC16 cells. SARS CoV 2 Spike pseudotyped particles were labeled with fluorescent quantum dots, and images were captured using highly inclined and laminated optical sheet fluorescence microscopy, also known as HILO microscopy. The particle trajectories were then analyzed to measure their distance, speed, and movement toward the center of the cell. Compared with control cells, increasing endosomal pH allowed the particles to travel farther and maintain inward movement for longer periods. These findings suggest that a higher endosomal pH may delay viral entry while allowing the particles to remain mobile for longer. In control cells, shorter travel distances may indicate earlier release of the viral genome. This work may help explain how endosomal pH coordinates the physical transport and biochemical maturation of virus containing compartments during SARS CoV 2 entry.Why this research mattersThe movement and maturation of virus containing endosomes are important steps in SARS CoV 2 infection. These findings suggest that endosomal pH may coordinate the movement of viral particles with the biochemical changes required for viral entry and genome release. Understanding this relationship could help identify new strategies for disrupting infection.

source_records.abstract: This research, conducted in the University of Michigan Dearborn Biophysics Lab, examines how endosomal acidity influences the movement of SARS CoV 2 particles inside human cardiomyocyte like cells. title: Comparative Evaluation of the Inactivation of SARS-CoV-2 and Human Coronavirus 229E against Sodium Hypochlorite
abstract: Introduction: Surface disinfection is one of the important non-pharmaceutical intervention measures that help prevent the spread of Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). Disinfectants with an efficacy claim against Human Coronavirus strain 229E (HCoV-229E) have been used for the disinfection of SARS-CoV-2; however, the comparative susceptibility of these two viruses to chemical disinfection has not been well defined. To address this, laboratory data were generated to compare the level of inactivation of human coronaviruses HCoV-229E and SARS-CoV-2 to a common antimicrobial agent, sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl), on a hard non-porous surface. Methods: A hard surface-based Quantitative Method (QM) was used to evaluate the viral inactivation efficacy by three treatments of NaOCl against HCoV-229E and SARS-CoV-2. For each treatment, viral inoculum containing soil load was applied onto a stainless steel carrier and dried. The inoculated carrier was exposed to NaOCl or a control fluid and held for five minutes. Following the exposure time, a neutralizer was added, and the sample was serially diluted and inoculated onto host cells to determine the number of infective units. The resulting Log10 of the density for control and treated carriers was used to generate Log10 reduction (LR) values for comparative statistical evaluation. Results: The mean LR ± standard error (SE) for HCoV-229E was 0.96 ± 0.09 (n=10) at 500 ppm NaOCl, 2.41 ± 0.15 (n=10) at 1,000 ppm NaOCl, and 4.54 ± 0.13 (n=10) at 1,500 ppm NaOCl. The mean LR ± SE for SARS-CoV-2 was 0.91 ± 0.24 (n=4) at 500 ppm NaOCl, 1.96 ± 0.26 (n=4) at 1,000 ppm NaOCl, and 4.23 ± 0.16 (n=4) at 1,500 ppm NaOCl. Both viruses were significantly responsive to the increasing concentrations of NaOCl. HCoV-229E had slightly higher mean LRs compared to SARS-CoV-2 at each NaOCl concentration; however, these differences were not statistically significant (p ≥ 0.067). Regression analysis using a linear mixed effects model (LMM) also indicates that the susceptibility of HCoV-229E and SARS-CoV-2 to NaOCl is comparable. Discussion: Understanding the antimicrobial tolerance of viruses can enhance public health response to viral infections. By determining the tolerance, the most appropriate antimicrobial agent can be chosen to disinfect surfaces contaminated with viral particles. Disinfection of highcontact surfaces can reduce the amount of fomite transmission and limit outbreaks. Conclusion: The data suggest that HCoV-229E and SARS-CoV-2 are statistically comparable in their susceptibility to NaOCl treatments.

title: EVALUATION OF THE DEVELOPMENT OF DIGITAL SKILLS IN ITLAC STUDENTS POST-COVID-19 PANDEMIC
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic highlighted the difficulties students and teachers faced in adapting to online education. This research evaluated the evolution of digital skills among Industrial Engineering students at TecNM - Lázaro Cárdenas, comparing the levels recorded at the beginning of the pandemic with a new measurement taken in 2025, with the aim of identifying significant changes and areas of opportunity to strengthen online and blended learning. A quantitative, descriptive study of population trends was conducted using independent samples. A survey based on a previously validated instrument with a five-level Likert scale was used. The population consisted of students from the Industrial Engineering program; 96 valid responses were obtained. The data were processed using Excel and SPSS version 25, comparing the 2025 results with those obtained in 2020. To determine if the observed differences between the two periods were statistically significant, a mean comparison test using the Z-statistics was applied. The overall average increased from 2.73 to 3.19. The one-tailed statistical test yielded a Z-value of 6.86, exceeding the critical value of 1.645 with α = 0.05, thus rejecting the null hypothesis and identifying a statistically significant increase among the analyzed measurements. Specialty competencies showed the greatest average increase (27%), followed by academic (19%) and generic (12%) competencies. The results confirm a statistically significant increase in digital skills following the pandemic. The main contribution of this study lies in the paradox identified in specialized skills: although they registered the greatest relative growth (27%), they continue to be the lowest in absolute terms (2.99 out of 5.00) compared to generic (3.40) and academic (3.07) skills. It is concluded that experience in virtual environments consolidated communication and transversal skills, but is insufficient for mastering advanced engineering technologies, which necessitates specific and intentional curricular strategies for blended learning.
journal: Veredas do Direito Direito Ambiental e Desenvolvimento Sustentável

title: Self-Medication During the COVID-19 Pandemic: A Scoping Review
abstract: This research project aims to conduct a scoping review of the available scientific evidence on self-medication during the COVID-19 pandemic. The review will systematically identify, map, and summarize studies reporting the prevalence of self-medication, its main characteristics and patterns, the medications and other health products most frequently used without professional prescription or supervision, and the individual, social, demographic, clinical, and contextual factors associated with this practice. The review will include relevant primary studies conducted during the COVID-19 pandemic in different populations and geographic settings. Particular attention will be given to variations in the prevalence and patterns of self-medication according to population characteristics, study setting, geographic region, and type of medication used. The review will also explore the motivations for self-medication, sources of information influencing medication use, access to healthcare services, perceived risk of COVID-19, and other factors reported as potentially associated with this behavior. The study will follow established methodological guidance for scoping reviews and will use a structured and transparent process for literature searching, study selection, data extraction, and evidence synthesis. Findings will be presented using descriptive tables, figures, and narrative synthesis to provide a comprehensive overview of the available literature. The expected outcomes are to characterize the extent and nature of self-medication during the COVID-19 pandemic, identify the medications and therapeutic groups most commonly used, summarize the factors associated with this practice, describe methodological characteristics of the existing evidence, and identify important knowledge gaps. The results may help inform future research, public health strategies, medication-safety interventions, and health communication policies aimed at reducing inappropriate or potentially harmful self-medication practices during public health emergencies.

title: Reconciliation of titer differences between SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing antibody assays
abstract: ABSTRACT SARS-CoV-2 antibody neutralization is a correlate of protection for COVID-19 and has been used to guide public health decisions. However, there is no standard neutralization assay, and absolute titers differ between assays. To investigate mechanisms causing these absolute titer differences, we compared 28 samples with three assays: a live virus cytopathic effect (CPE)-based microneutralization assay, a live virus focus reduction (immunospot, IS) assay, and a pseudotyped virus luciferase expression reduction (pseudovirus, PV) assay. We found significant correlations between all assays (ρ > 0.95 and P t -tests P IMPORTANCE Protection against COVID-19 is related to how well serum antibodies neutralize SARS-CoV-2. This neutralization can be assessed using different assays, which often provide significantly different estimates. To better understand why assay results vary, we compared three commonly used types of neutralization assay. We found both strong correlations and significant differences in measured neutralization between the different assays. Differences in the type of virus (live SARS-CoV-2 virus compared to a pseudotyped virus with SARS-CoV-2 spike protein), how long cells, virus, and antibody were allowed to interact, and whether neutralization of a batch of virions (“per well” neutralization) or individual infectious virions (“per virion”) was measured, all impacted virus neutralization. Understanding which factors have the largest impact on the differences between neutralization assays is an important first step toward harmonization of neutralization assays across the field.

title: Advancing Health Equity In Long Covid: Bioethical Considerations And System-Level Strategies For Post-Acute Care And Recovery
abstract: Abstract: Long COVID has emerged as a continuing public health challenge, with symptoms such as fatigue, cognitive slowing and shortness of breath affecting many people well after the initial SARS-CoV-2 infection. This review synthesizes evidence on prevalence, symptom, risk determinants, health utilization, and the wider social and economic effects of Long COVID, emphasizing prevention and health system preparedness. The analysis highlights differences across regions and population groups, rising pressure on rehabilitation services and notable consequences for employment, education and mental health. The study looks at fairness in resource distribution within overburdened health systems, equity in care access, and the protection of vulnerable groups in research and policy responses from an ethical standpoint. We underline the importance of harmonized diagnostic criteria, inclusive and representative research, and equitable access to chronic care services. We also set out priority policy actions to support earlier identification, team-based models of care and coordinated national strategies. By integrating clinical, economic and social perspectives, this review outlines a policy priorities to support early identification, multidisciplinary care, and coordinated national strategies. We also examine bioethical considerations including equity in care access, resource allocation in strained health systems, and protection of vulnerable populations in research and policy responses.

title: The Impact of Extended COVID-19 Lockdowns on Scottish Residents’ Mental Health
abstract: This article will explore Michel Foucault’s ideas with respect to the coronavirus pandemic (COVID-19), focusing on biopolitics and the influence of the surveillance state. The impact of extended and extensive lockdowns on the mental health of Scottish residents is scrutinized from a Foucauldian perspective. A key limitation of using Foucault’s framework for analysing the pandemic must be recognized. While Foucault’s perspective focuses on control mechanisms, it might lead to viewing all public health measures with suspicion. For example, the UK’s vaccination campaign was said to have prevented approximately 100,000 deaths, demonstrating that biopower can be beneficial, not solely oppressive. The framework is most useful not as a comprehensive critique but to challenge uncomfortable assumptions about who wields power, whose lives are valued, and how consent is created. In this way, it remains a vital perspective for understanding not only COVID-19, but also the broader dynamics between governance, bodies, and society.
journal: International Journal of Mental Health Research

title: ATTITUDES AND PRACTICES TOWARDS COVID-19 AND SEASONAL FLU VACCINES AND VACCINATION IN THE GENERAL POPULATION AND AMONG MEDICAL PROFESSIONALS
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has led to the development of several types of vaccines, among which messenger RNA (mRNA)-based vaccines have represented a significant breakthrough. This study aimed to evaluate attitudes towards COVID-19 and seasonal influenza vaccination among the general population and individuals with a medical background. A questionnaire was developed to collect sociodemographic data, personal health information, vaccination status, and information on participants’ attitudes towards and knowledge of vaccines. The profile of the typical participant was an employed woman with tertiary education, living with another person in an urban area and reporting generally good health. The typical participant had received at least two doses of the Sputnik V vaccine. Participants generally expressed favourable attitudes towards regular COVID-19 vaccination. The results showed no apparent differences between participants with and without a medical background regarding vaccine choice, the decision to receive a third dose, or seasonal influenza vaccination. Similarly, no apparent differences were observed in attitudes towards the AstraZeneca vaccine or mandatory COVID-19 vaccination between respondents with and without a medical background.

title: ASSESSMENT OF ADVERSE DRUG REACTIONS FOLLOWING COVID-19 VACCINATION AMONG UNDERGRADUATE HEALTHCARE STUDENTS: A CROSS-SECTIONAL STUDY
abstract: Objective: The present investigation aimed to examine adverse drug reactions (ADRs) reported after COVID-19 vaccination among undergraduate healthcare students. It also evaluated the occurrence, clinical characteristics, and duration of adverse events experienced following immunization. Methods: A questionnaire-based descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among undergraduate healthcare students of Gyani Inder Singh Institute of Professional Studies, Dehradun, Uttarakhand, India. A structured questionnaire consisting of 14 close-ended questions was used to collect demographic information, vaccination status, type of vaccine received, occurrence of adverse reactions, symptom duration, and post-vaccination outcomes. A total of 26 valid responses were included in the final analysis. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and expressed as numbers and percentages. Results: Among the participants, 88.5% were pharmacy students and 96.2% were male. Covishield was the most commonly administered vaccine (84.6%), followed by Covaxin (11.5%). Most participants had completed booster-dose vaccination (65.4%). Adverse drug reactions following vaccination were reported by 80.8% of participants. The most common adverse reactions included pain at the injection site (69.2%), fever (53.8%), fatigue (50%), myalgia (46.2%), headache (38.5%), and chills (30.8%). Most symptoms resolved within one to four days. A small proportion of participants reported breakthrough COVID-19 infection after vaccination. No serious or life-threatening adverse reactions were reported. Conclusion: The results suggest that COVID-19 vaccination had a favorable safety profile among undergraduate healthcare students. source_records.abstract: Objective: The present investigation aimed to examine adverse drug reactions (ADRs) reported after COVID-19 vaccination among undergraduate healthcare students. It also evaluated the occurrence, clinical characteristics, and duration of adverse events experienced following immunization. Methods: A questionnaire-based descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among undergraduate healthcare students of Gyani Inder Singh Institute of Professional Studies, Dehradun, Uttarakhand, India. A structured questionnaire consisting of 14 close-ended questions was used to collect demographic information, vaccination status, type of vaccine received, occurrence of adverse reactions, symptom duration, and post-vaccination outcomes. A total of 26 valid responses were included in the final analysis. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and expressed as numbers and percentages. Results: Among the participants, 88.5% were pharmacy students and 96.2% were male. Covishield was the most commonly administered vaccine (84.6%), followed by Covaxin (11.5%). Most participants had completed booster-dose vaccination (65.4%). Adverse drug reactions following vaccination were reported by 80.8% of participants. No serious or life-threatening adverse reactions were reported. Conclusion: The results suggest that COVID-19 vaccination had a favorable safety profile among undergraduate healthcare students. The reported adverse events were predominantly minor, resolved within a short period, and generally required no specific intervention. Nevertheless, continued monitoring of vaccine-related reactions and effective pharmacovigilance are important for identifying safety concerns, supporting reliable safety data, and sustaining confidence in vaccination programs.
