title: The commercialization of "unvaccinated" blood: A cross-sectional analysis of organizations marketing services based on donor COVID-19 vaccination status.
abstract: BACKGROUND Requests for blood from donors not vaccinated against COVID-19 persist despite evidence that donor vaccination does not affect transfusion recipients. We characterized organizations marketing services based on donor vaccination status. STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of publicly available websites from organizations marketing access to unvaccinated blood. Between July 25 and July 26, 2026, we performed 30 prespecified Google searches in six languages and screened the first 50 results per query. We included organizations offering enrollment, paid access, documents, donor registration, matching, or assistance based on COVID-19 vaccination status. We coded geographic reach, payment, services, donor classification, diagnostic claims, blood handling, and operational limitations. RESULTS Eight organizations met inclusion criteria; four described international reach. All marketed an existing or planned donor registry or matching service, seven charged fees or offered paid access, six issued patient-facing documents, and seven advertised clinician directories, referrals, advocacy, or legal support. Donor status was classified through self-report, records, declarations, exemptions, social media screenshots, membership identification, or trust. One organization promoted unvalidated diagnostic tests. All depended on external clinicians, hospitals, or blood establishments; none described collecting, testing, processing, or storing blood components. Several acknowledged that matching was unavailable or not guaranteed or that hospital acceptance varied. DISCUSSION Organizations are monetizing vaccine misinformation by selling memberships, documents, donor registries, professional directories, and advocacy services. These products give vaccination status the appearance of a medically meaningful blood attribute and may channel unsupported directed donation requests to hospitals and blood establishments.

title: Losartan with add-on spironolactone for severe COVID-19 in the intensive care unit: a randomized controlled trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND The Coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic caused significant mortality, predominantly among patients with comorbidities. Management of critically ill patients relies mainly on supportive care. SARS-CoV-2 influences the renin-angiotensin system, a potential therapeutic target. The aim was to evaluate whether losartan and spironolactone, added to standard care, improve organ failure and other clinical outcomes in patients with severe COVID-19 admitted to intensive care units. We designed a randomized, open-label, parallel-group trial, in five intensive care units in Marseille, France, from September 2020 to September 2021. METHODS Adults with COVID-19-related respiratory distress were randomized. The experimental group received standard care plus losartan and conditional addition of spironolactone for 10 days while the control group received standard care alone. The primary endpoint was the SOFA-score on day 7. Secondary endpoints included SOFA scores at other time points, intubation rates, mechanical ventilation duration, 90-day mortality, viral replication, and safety. RESULTS 78 patients were randomized (39 in the control group, 39 in the experimental group); the primary outcome was analysed in 73 patients (the modified intention-to-treat population comprised 74; one experimental patient died on day 6). We found no significant difference in median SOFA-score on day 7 between the groups (3 vs 2; p = 0.5). There were no significant differences in intubation rates, mechanical ventilation duration, 90-day mortality, or adverse events. Viral replication and oxygenation parameters were also similar. CONCLUSION This trial did not detect a statistically significant treatment effect of losartan, with spironolactone added in a minority of patients, on clinical outcomes in COVID-19 ICU patients. However, the trial was underpowered due to early termination.

title: Investigating the association between COVID-19 exposure and fetal and maternal health before public health vaccinations: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract: OBJECTIVES Pregnant women and neonates face a higher risk of adverse outcomes from infectious diseases, such as COVID-19. COVID-19 vaccines were developed rapidly, but we do not fully understand how the disease affected pregnancies and births before these vaccines were available. This study investigated how COVID-19 impact on pregnant women and their neonates before vaccines became widely available. The aim was to investigate the association between maternal COVID-19 infection and pregnancy and neonatal outcomes. STUDY DESIGN This retrospective cohort study included pregnant women and their neonates (n = 3472 each) in Mashhad before the COVID-19 vaccine rollout. METHODS Participants were categorized into two groups: those who had COVID-19 and those who did not. Chi-square, t-tests, and Fisher's exact test were used to compare the groups. Linear and logistic regression analyses were used to examine the associations between COVID-19 exposure and different outcomes, both before and after adjusting for potential confounders. RESULTS Pregnant women with COVID-19, when compared to those without, experienced less weight gain (OR = 0.91, CI 95%: 0.82-0.93) and shorter pregnancy duration (OR = 0.95, CI 95%: 0.92-0.97). COVID-19 infection in pregnant women also showed links to higher odds of cesarean (OR = 1.72, CI 95%: 1.62-1.83), gestational diabetes (OR = 1.11, CI 95%: 1.007-1.22), and unusual newborns that had congenital abnormalities (OR = 1.46, CI 95%: 1.03-2.11). CONCLUSION The study indicates that women who had COVID-19 during pregnancy, before vaccines were available, had a higher risk of adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes. This finding can provide useful information to healthcare providers and pregnant women about how COVID-19 vaccination can reduce the severity of illness and adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes during pregnancy and the postnatal period.

title: Prevalência da Perda de Memória Autorreferida após a COVID-19 e Fatores Associados
abstract: Enquadramento: A identificação da perda de memória após a fase aguda da infeção por SARS-CoV-2 é importante para a gestão dos cuidados, devido ao impacto nas atividades da vida diária. Objetivo: Determinar a prevalência da perda de memória autorreferida em pessoas com condição pós-COVID-19 e identificar os fatores associados. Metodologia: Estudo quantitativo, observacional e transversal, cujos dados foram recolhidos junto de residentes do Norte do Brasil com 18 ou mais anos que autorreferiram diagnóstico comprovado por exame de infeção por SARS-CoV-2 e condição pós-COVID-19. Foi aplicado um questionário online adaptado. Resultados: A prevalência da perda de memória autorreferida após a COVID-19 foi de 53,3% (366), estando associada à idade, ao sexo, ao ano do primeiro exame confirmativo da infeção por SARS-CoV-2, ao diagnóstico de COVID-19 antes da primeira vacina, ao número de infeções por SARS-CoV-2 e aos medicamentos usados para tratar a COVID-19, como antibióticos, antivirais, ivermectina e remédios caseiros. Conclusão: O rastreio precoce é importante para orientar o cuidado e o autocuidado da população afetada.

title: Left behind places and regional resilience to COVID-19 shock in Europe
abstract: Current turbulent times pose challenges not only for countries, but also-and above all-for regions within them. However, economic resilience of left behind places is still underexplored, especially in the light of entrenched regional disparities. The aim of this paper is to investigate the nexus between regional development and economic resilience across 898 European NUTS 3 regions during the COVID-19 pandemic. To go beyond the GDP-based approach, we construct a multidimensional "left behindness" index. Our findings show that left-behind places, as identified through this multidimensional approach, were relatively more successful in resisting the immediate pandemic shock, while more developed regions demonstrated a stronger recovery capacity. The analysis also highlights that international trade, industrial specialization and the share of public employment acted as determinants of these divergent resilience trajectories. The results suggest that policymakers should adopt a differentiated strategy by strengthening the resistance of more advanced regions and enhancing the recovery capacity of left behind places to reduce persistent regional disparities.

title: THE IMPACT OF COVID-19 PANDEMIC ON SOCIAL CAPITAL INEQUALITIES ACROSS INCOME GROUPS: EVIDENCE FROM TÜRKİYE
abstract: This study examines social capital differences across income groups in Türkiye and empirically analyzes the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on these differences. The study employs LPM and Probit models using repeated cross-sectional (pooled) micro data from the Turkish Statistical Institute's Life Satisfaction Survey for 2017–2022. Social capital is measured by whether individuals have access to an informal support network of relatives, friends, or neighbors in times of need. The findings reveal a strong positive relationship between household income and social capital. The highest-income group exhibits roughly 9 percentage points higher social capital than the lowest-income group. The pandemic dramatically widened this gap. The intergroup difference increased from approximately 5 percentage points in 2017 to 13 percentage points in 2021, nearly tripling social capital inequality. While the lowest-income group experienced substantial erosion of its informal networks, the highest-income group largely preserved its social capital.
journal: Anadolu Üniversitesi İktisadi ve İdari Bilimler Fakültesi Dergisi

title: Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus in the COVID-19 Era: A Descriptive Cross-Sectional Study from Al-Jabal Al-Akhdar, Libya
abstract: Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) requires lifelong insulin therapy. The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic may have affected diabetes presentation and care directly through infection and indirectly through disrupted access to health services. This study described selected clinical characteristics of people with T1DM followed at a government diabetes center in eastern Libya and examined the temporal context of COVID-19 in the available records. We conducted a retrospective, descriptive cross-sectional review of 126 records from the Educational Diabetes Center in Al-Jabal Al-Akhdar, Libya, covering November 2017 through March 2022. The source data did not indicate whether the 126 records represented unique individuals or included repeat visits; therefore, all denominators are record-based. The analysis summarized counts and percentages, and calendar-period counts were also expressed as averages per observed month to account for the partial coverage of 2017 and 2022. No inferential tests were performed. Of 126 records, 51 (40.5%) were dated 2021, equivalent to 4.25 records per observed month. Renal impairment was recorded in 6 records (4.8%), myopia in 17 (13.5%), a previous viral infection in 2 (1.6%), an associated condition in 2 (1.6%), injection-site lipodystrophy in 1 (0.8%), and hyperlipidemia in 2 (1.6%). A family history of confirmed COVID-19 before diabetes onset was recorded in 3 records (2.4%); all described female patients who reportedly presented with diabetic ketoacidosis approximately three months after the family infection. The dataset documents a small number of T1DM presentations after reported household COVID-19 exposure. Because exposure was based on family history, patient infection was not established, record uniqueness could not be verified, and the design lacked a population denominator or non-T1DM control group, the findings do not demonstrate that COVID-19 caused or increased the risk of T1DM. Larger controlled studies with verified exposure and standardized outcome definitions are required.
journal: AlQalam Journal of Medical and Applied Sciences

source_records.title: Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus in the COVID-19 Era: A Descriptive Cross-Sectional Study from Al-Jabal Al-Akhdar, Libya
source_records.abstract: Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) requires lifelong insulin therapy. The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic may have affected diabetes presentation and care directly through infection and indirectly through disrupted access to health services. This study described selected clinical characteristics of people with T1DM followed at a government diabetes center in eastern Libya and examined the temporal context of COVID-19 in the available records. We conducted a retrospective, descriptive cross-sectional review of 126 records from the Educational Diabetes Center in Al-Jabal Al-Akhdar, Libya, covering November 2017 through March 2022. The source data did not indicate whether the 126 records represented unique individuals or included repeat visits; therefore, all denominators are record-based. The analysis summarized counts and percentages, and calendar-period counts were also expressed as averages per observed month to account for the partial coverage of 2017 and 2022. No inferential tests were performed. Of 126 records, 51 (40.5%) were dated 2021, equivalent to 4.25 records per observed month. Renal impairment was recorded in 6 records (4.8%), myopia in 17 (13.5%), a previous viral infection in 2 (1.6%), an associated condition in 2 (1.6%), injection-site lipodystrophy in 1 (0.8%), and hyperlipidemia in 2 (1.6%). A family history of confirmed COVID-19 before diabetes onset was recorded in 3 records (2.4%); all described female patients who reportedly presented with diabetic ketoacidosis approximately three months after the family infection. The dataset documents a small number of T1DM presentations after reported household COVID-19 exposure. Because exposure was based on family history, patient infection was not established, record uniqueness could not be verified, and the design lacked a population denominator or non-T1DM control group, the findings do not demonstrate that COVID-19 caused or increased the risk of T1DM. Larger controlled studies with verified exposure and standardized outcome definitions are required.

title: Tax-Benefit Responses in Uruguay During the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: Abstract We analyze the social protection policy response to COVID-19 and its impact on household incomes in Uruguay during 2020 and 2021, using static microsimulation methods. From the onset of the crisis, the Uruguayan government implemented adjustments to existing social protection policies as well as a new transfer and an emergency tax. Our results indicate that Uruguay’s enhanced social protection system prevented poverty from increasing by 2.8 and 3.7 percentage points in 2020 and 2021, respectively. The COVID-19 enhancements contributed 1.3 and 1.6 percentage points of this total protective effect. The effects were bigger among households with children. The most important instruments were unemployment insurance in 2020 and the conditional cash transfer directed at households with children in 2021. Taken together, these modifications to the social protection system prevented the Gini index from increasing by around 0.7 additional percentage points.

title: POST-COVID-19 CONDITION (LONG COVID): INFLAMMATORY MECHANISMS, ENDOTHELIAL DYSFUNCTION, AND PERSISTENCE OF MULTISYSTEM SYMPTOMS
abstract: Post-COVID-19 condition, also known as Long COVID, is characterized by persistent or newly developed clinical manifestations following the acute phase of SARS-CoV-2 infection and may affect multiple organs and systems. This review aimed to analyze contemporary evidence regarding inflammatory mechanisms, endothelial dysfunction, and their potential relationship with persistent multisystem symptoms in post-COVID-19 condition. An integrative literature review was conducted using PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect, covering publications from September 2021 to September 2026. A total of 731 records were identified and, after screening and eligibility assessment, 14 studies were included in the final qualitative synthesis. Current evidence indicates a heterogeneous and probably multifactorial pathophysiology involving persistent immune activation, increased inflammatory mediators, prolonged detection of viral components, complement abnormalities, and endothelial and microvascular dysfunction. Clinical studies have also demonstrated associations between vascular impairment and fatigue, chest pain, exercise intolerance, and neurocognitive manifestations. However, no single biological mechanism explains the entire clinical spectrum. Long COVID should therefore be understood as a multisystem condition resulting from interactions among immunological, vascular, metabolic, and potentially persistent viral mechanisms.
authors: Eberson da Silva Rodrigues do Nascimento

title: Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic on India and it’s Neighbouring Countries: An MSME Perspective
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic triggered an unprecedented global economic disruption, leading to sharp contractions in output, employment, and cross-border economic activity. While the global economic effects of the pandemic have been widely documented, comparatively less attention has been devoted to its differentiated impacts on India’s neighbouring countries, particularly from a Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) perspective. This study examines the pandemic’s economic impact on selected neighbouring countries of India, with a specific focus on MSMEs, which play a crucial role in employment generation and economic activity across the region. Using secondary data from international statistical sources and country-level reports, the study analyses cross-country variations in GDP growth performance and documented disruptions faced by MSMEs during the pandemic period. The findings reveal substantial heterogeneity in the depth of economic contraction and recovery patterns across countries, reflecting differences in sectoral dependence, exposure to external shocks, and policy responses. The study contributes to a region-specific understanding of the pandemic’s economic consequences and underscores the importance of strengthening MSME resilience to enhance preparedness for future systemic shocks.

title: CONDIÇÃO PÓS-COVID-19 (LONG COVID): MECANISMOS INFLAMATÓRIOS, DISFUNÇÃO ENDOTELIAL E PERSISTÊNCIA DE SINTOMAS MULTISSISTÊMICOS
abstract: A condição pós-COVID-19, também denominada COVID longa ou Long COVID, caracteriza-se pela persistência ou surgimento de manifestações clínicas após a fase aguda da infecção pelo SARS-CoV-2, podendo comprometer diferentes órgãos e sistemas. O objetivo desta revisão foi analisar as evidências contemporâneas sobre os mecanismos inflamatórios, a disfunção endotelial e sua possível relação com a persistência de sintomas multissistêmicos na condição pós-COVID-19. Realizou-se revisão integrativa da literatura, com busca nas bases PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science e ScienceDirect, considerando publicações entre setembro de 2021 e setembro de 2026. Foram identificados 731 registros e, após as etapas de triagem e elegibilidade, 14 estudos compuseram a síntese qualitativa final. As evidências demonstram fisiopatologia heterogênea e provavelmente multifatorial, envolvendo ativação imunológica persistente, aumento de mediadores inflamatórios, presença prolongada de componentes virais, alterações do sistema complemento e comprometimento endotelial e microvascular. Estudos clínicos também demonstraram associação entre alterações vasculares e manifestações como fadiga, dor torácica, intolerância ao esforço e comprometimento neurocognitivo. Entretanto, nenhum mecanismo isolado explica todos os fenótipos clínicos. Conclui-se que a condição pós-COVID-19 deve ser compreendida como uma síndrome multissistêmica resultante da interação entre processos imunológicos, vasculares, metabólicos e possivelmente relacionados à persistência viral.
authors: Eberson da Silva Rodrigues do Nascimento

title: Teaching human geography fieldwork during COVID-19: Challenges and new possibilities
abstract: Fieldwork has long been a cornerstone of geographical research, and field courses have likewise served as an essential means of engaging with the key issues that define the discipline, both in physical and human geography. In human geography field courses, students learn to use qualitative methods such as interviews and participant observation among people. In this intervention paper I discuss what practical challenges the COVID-19 pandemic posed to the organisation of a field course in human geography in the University of Oulu in Finland, during spring 2020. The key questions and challenges back then were how the main idea of leaving the university classrooms and going among the people to learn geography was even possible at the same time when governments around the globe strongly advised people to stay home and avoid human connections. Regardless of the challenges, the field course was organised. In the course, students managed to come up with creative solutions to achieve the course's learning goals and learn to use qualitative methods in practice. The course required the redefinition for the concept of ‘field’, which at the same time challenged geography’s disciplinary history.

title: Epigenetic regulation of DPP4 receptor expression by NONO enables replication of MERS-CoV
abstract: Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus (MERS-CoV), first reported in 2012, belongs to the Betacoronavirus genus, including SARS-CoV and SARS-CoV-2. Human-to-human transmission of MERS-CoV appears inefficient, but repeated spillover events have been reported from at least 27 countries, raising concern for future emergent events. Coronaviruses (CoVs) rely extensively on host proteins to support their replication. Several studies have implicated the paraspeckle non-POU domain-containing octamer-binding protein (NONO) as an RNA-binding protein (RBP) that binds to CoV genomes, but the role of this protein in regulating replication is unknown. Here, we show that NONO is required for expression of dipeptidyl peptidase 4 (DPP4, also known as CD26), the major cellular receptor required for MERS-CoV attachment and entry. NONO did not impact DPP4 mRNA processing or stability but instead promoted DPP4 transcription through control of active H3K4me3 and repressive H3K27me3 histone modifications at the DPP4 locus. Together, these findings identify NONO as a key proviral host factor for MERS-CoV and reveal an epigenetic mechanism linking a host RBP to viral entry receptor expression that may represent a target for therapeutic strategies.

title: Mortality Surveillance Learning Module: Durán et al (2026), Multiple causes of death data to track trends of mortality from chronic diseases: Insights from the COVID-19 pandemic in Switzerland.
abstract: Educational Engagement Modules (EEMs) are teaching materials for educators and students that facilitate a deeper understanding of key epidemiological methods and concepts. Each EEM poses a series of questions using a recently published paper in Annals to further understanding of a specific study design or epidemiological concept and to encourage critical thinking and careful evaluation. This EEM focuses on mortality surveillance featuring the following article: Durán N D, Kaufman JS, Chiolero A, Carmeli C. Multiple causes of death data to track trends of mortality from chronic diseases: Insights from the COVID-19 pandemic in Switzerland. doi: 10.1016/j.annepidem.2025.12.002.

title: Критерії диференційної діагностики туберкульозу легень і негоспітальної пневмонії середньотяжкого та тяжкого перебігу, асоційованої з COVID-19. Частина 2
abstract: The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, particularly during its early stages, was characterised by the rapid spread of SARS-CoV-2 infection, which triggered activation of the immune system followed by its subsequent exhaustion. As a result, immune control over Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB) was impaired, especially in regions with a high tuberculosis burden and a significant prevalence of latent tuberculosis (TB) infection. These changes may have contributed to a more severe course of tuberculosis and potentially increa­sed the risk of developing resistance to anti-tuberculosis drugs. Objective — to evaluate the relationship between the clinical severity, the cell-mediated immune response, endogenous intoxication, and nitro-oxidative stress in patients with pulmonary tuberculosis, infected with different strains of MTB and concomitant SARS-CoV-2. Materials and methods. A prospective study included 191 newly diagnosed patients with pulmonary TB, distributed into four groups: the 1st study group (1st SG) included 80 patients with drug-susceptible TB, the 2nd study group (2nd SG) comprised 40 patients with primary multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB), the 3rd study group (3rd SG) consisted of 49 patients with acquired MDR-TB, and the 4th study group (4th SG) included 22 patients (11 with drug-susceptible TB and 11 with primary MDR-TB) co-infected with SARS-CoV-2. The indices were compared with those of a control group (CG) of 36 conventionally healthy individuals. The laboratory investigations included immunophenotyping of CD3+, CD4+, CD8+, and CD19+ cells, C-reactive protein, ceruloplasmin, circulating immune complexes (CICs), tumour necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), interleu­kin-6 (IL-6) and interleukin-8 (IL-8), leukocyte and hematologic intoxication indices, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR). Biomarkers of nitro-oxidative stress included nitric oxide metabolites (NOx), advanced oxidation protein products (AOPP), advanced glycation end products (AGE), myeloperoxidase (MPO), N-acetyl-β-D-glucosaminidase (NAG) and malondialdehyde (MDA). Results and discussion. Clinical-radiological findings indicated a more severe TB evolution in patients with acquired MDR-TB and those co-infected with SARS-CoV-2, supported by depletion of CD3+, CD4+, CD8+ and CD16+ cells, and strong negative correlations between immune cell levels and disease severity. Elevated CIC-2.5 % and CIC-4.2 %, with increased ESR and acute-phase proteins (C-reactive protein and ceruloplas­min), indicated sustained immune activation and strong associations with disease severity, whereas CIC-8.0 % showed weaker correlations due to rapid systemic clearance. Increased pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-8, and IL-6) and elevated nitro-oxidative stress markers (NOx, MDA, AOPP, AGEs, NAG, MPO) indicated intensified neutrophil-driven inflammation, systemic inflammatory response, and pronounced lipid, protein, and cellular damage in acquired MDR-TB and concomitant SARS-CoV-2 coinfection. Acquired MDR-TB and SARS-CoV-2 co-infection determine severe clinical-radiological evolution, pronounced cell-mediated immune depletion, sustained immune complex formation and acute-phase activation, intensified cytokine-driven inflammation and nitro-oxidative stress, overall contributing to enhanced immune dysregulation.

title: Leading in the shadows: contextualising educational leadership and EdTech innovations in Pakistan during COVID-19
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic exposed the inadequacy of globally dominant educational technology (EdTech) models for education systems in the Global South, where assumptions of connectivity, device ownership, and digital literacy did not hold. This article examines how educational leaders in Pakistan navigated these conditions, asking two related questions: how did educational leaders operate in the shadows of universalised EdTech models during Pakistan's COVID-19 crisis, and what do their practices of improvisation and care reveal about the situated and relational nature of educational leadership? Grounded in a critical phenomenological and autoethnographic design, the study draws on three narrative vignettes — one autobiographical account of the national TeleSchool television initiative and two crafted narratives developed from semi-structured interviews with two school principals — read through the dual lenses of Foucauldian subjectivation and Merleau-Ponty's phenomenology of embodiment. The analysis advances three interconnected arguments. First, dominant EdTech paradigms demonstrate systematic misalignment with the conditions of the Global South, as Pakistan's contextually grounded pivot to television rather than internet-based platforms illustrates. Second, educational leadership in crisis is a situated, ethical, and often invisible labour, enacted through embodied improvisation, relational care, and moral commitment in the spaces policy and technology cannot reach — a mode of practice the article names leadership in the shadows : spatially marginal, ethically driven, embodied, and structurally invisible, yet foundational to sustaining education in crisis. Third, and as a distinct normative contribution, the article proposes a relational ethics of leadership : a framework for reconnecting centralised policy with the lived knowledge of frontline leaders. The article's central conceptual contribution is thus the theorisation of leadership in the shadows as a lived phenomenon attuned to the nuances of fragile contexts such as Pakistan. Offered as an exploratory and conceptual account rather than a generalisable model, the study contributes to scholarship on decolonising educational leadership and EdTech narratives, and calls for educational futures grounded in equity, care, and contextual intelligence.

Second, educational leadership in crisis is a situated, ethical, and often invisible labour, enacted through embodied improvisation, relational care, and moral commitment in the spaces policy and technology cannot reach — a mode of practice the article names leadership in the shadows : spatially marginal, ethically driven, embodied, and structurally invisible, yet foundational to sustaining education in crisis. Third, and as a distinct normative contribution, the article proposes a relational ethics of leadership : a framework for reconnecting centralised policy with the lived knowledge of frontline leaders. The article's central conceptual contribution is thus the theorisation of leadership in the shadows as a lived phenomenon attuned to the nuances of fragile contexts such as Pakistan. Offered as an exploratory and conceptual account rather than a generalisable model, the study contributes to scholarship on decolonising educational leadership and EdTech narratives, and calls for educational futures grounded in equity, care, and contextual intelligence.

title: Covid-19 Döneminde Birleşme ve Satın Alma Duyurularının Fiyatlanması: Borsa İstanbul’da Volatilite Rejimlerinin Rolü Pricing of Merger and Acquisition Announcements During the COVID-19 Period: The Role of Volatility Regimes in Borsa Istanbul
abstract: Market reactions to merger and acquisition announcements may vary depending on both the informational content of the announcement and the market conditions prevailing at the time of disclosure. This study examines whether the price effects of merger and acquisition announcements made in Türkiye during the Covid-19 period differ across volatility regimes. For this purpose, the event study methodology is applied to announcements made by firms listed on Borsa Istanbul, and cumulative abnormal returns are calculated. The regime structure of market volatility is identified using a two-state Markov-switching GARCH model estimated from BIST100 index returns. The resulting regime probabilities are matched with event dates, and announcement effects are compared across low- and high-volatility regimes. The findings indicate that average cumulative abnormal returns around merger and acquisition announcements are generally positive but statistically insignificant. The results from short-term event windows and winsorization analyses also support this finding. Regime-based analyses show that market reactions tend to be more favorable during low-volatility periods, whereas they weaken or turn negative during high-volatility periods. However, the difference between the regimes is not statistically significant. The EGARCH results reveal a positive relationship between the probability of the high-volatility regime and conditional volatility, thereby supporting the economic interpretability of the regime classification. In this respect, the study provides an integrated analytical framework for evaluating merger and acquisition announcements under different market conditions by combining event study methodology with regime-based volatility models.

title: Reoviridae-derived short trimerization domain for stabilizing homo-trimerization of vaccine immunogens and therapeutic proteins
abstract: Trimerization motifs play pivotal roles in structural biology and therapeutic protein engineering. Here, we describe a short trimerization motif (rFd1303) derived from the Reoviridae family reovirus σ1 protein. Compared with the widely used T4-Foldon, the rFd1303 increased recombinant protein yields. The rFd1303-fused immunogens of SARS-CoV-2 spike and influenza hemagglutinin elicited antibody responses comparable to T4-Foldon-fused controls in mice. Using this tag, we engineered a trimeric ACE2-Ig fusion protein (TriACE2-Ig) that remained stable after 30 days at room temperature and neutralized a broad range of ACE2-utilizing sarbecoviruses, including 19 SARS-CoV-2 variants, SARS-CoV, and pangolin coronaviruses GD and GX, with higher potency than monomeric ACE2-Ig. In the hamster model challenged with various SARS-CoV-2 variants, our data demonstrated that intranasal TriACE2-Ig administration markedly reduced viral loads, virus-induced body-weight loss, lung pathology, and decreased within-cage virus transmission. These findings highlight rFd1303 as a versatile trimerization platform for vaccine and therapeutic protein development. In this study, the authors engineer a short trimerization tag for vaccine and therapeutic protein development. The tag enables a trimeric ACE2 decoy that exhibits broad neutralizing activity against coronaviruses and confers protection in animal models.

title: In Silico Variant Analysis Identifies Mutations in TP53 Gene Increasing The Risk of Cancer in COVID-19 Patients
abstract: Introduction: The Coronavirus 2019 (COVID-19) disease caused by SARS-CoV-2 emerged as a global pandemic due to its lethal nature and great potential to spread rapidly. It is predicted that the coronavirus infection can leave detrimental consequences in infected patients even after recovery. Therefore considering the ability of the virus to induce lethal mutations in the host genome, we aimed to identify variants in COVID-19 patients irrespective of their origin. Methods: For the present study, transcriptomic data of patients were retrieved from the GEO dataset of the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) (GSE216811 and GSE197976 (India), GSE174786 (Germany), GSE171052 (Canada), GSE 206264 (Spain) and GSE206677 (Japan)). Each dataset was assessed independently for Single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs). After quality check and removing low-quality reads the samples were normalized using Bcf-tools norms. Further, SnpEff eff and SIFT4g annotator was used to identify and annotate variants occurring in each sample. The common variants occurring in all the patients of COVID-19. Were identified through a Venn diagram. The systems biology approach was used to identify hub genes out of common mutated genes. Results and Discussion: CytoHUBBA plug-in of Cytoscape identified TP53 as the hub gene mutated due to COVID- 19 infection. TP53 is a tumor suppressor gene that plays an important role in DNA damage repair, cell cycle regulation, and inducing apoptosis. Conclusion: Therefore, we conclude that mutation in TP53 causes loss of suppression potential of the gene increasing the risk of cancer in such individuals.

title: The impact of COVID-19 on investors’ behavior: the case of anchoring and 52 week high
abstract: This paper aims to examine how the COVID-19 pandemic influenced investor behavior in Kuwait’s emerging market, focusing on changes in anchoring patterns tied to the 52-week high/low strategy. Using daily stock data from 2012 to 2024, the author find that investors typically favored momentum strategies anchored to 52-week highs. During the pandemic, however, a marked shift occurred in which investors gravitated toward stocks near their 52-week lows, likely perceiving them as undervalued or safer amid increased uncertainty. This contrarian shift proved profitable, with the 52-week low strategy outperforming during the crisis. Postpandemic, investor behavior largely reverted to momentum-based preferences. These findings highlight the temporary adaptability of anchoring heuristics under crisis conditions and offer novel insights into behavioral finance within the GCC context. The study underscores the importance of dynamic investor psychology in shaping market behavior during periods of systemic stress.

title: Context-specific strategies for enhancing HPV vaccination: key informant perspectives from selected U.S. jurisdictions in the post-COVID-19 era
abstract: Despite the availability of a safe and effective Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine, uptake remains inconsistent across the United States (U.S.), with marked differences in vaccination coverage across states. This descriptive exploratory study examined key informant perspectives on HPV vaccination promotion across policy-engaged jurisdictions in the U.S. in the post-COVID-19 era. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with nine key informants across six U.S. Classification of the interviews was based on those with existing HPV vaccine school-entry requirements or those jurisdictions with recent school-entry policy considerations. Using inductive thematic analysis, we synthesized key informant perspectives and organized themes using analytical dimensions informed by the socio-ecological model. Findings highlight the importance of provider education, school-entry requirements, cancer prevention messaging, trusted messengers, culturally tailored outreach, and cross-sector partnerships as important components of HPV vaccine promotion. Barriers such as vaccine misinformation and increased hesitancy following the COVID-19 pandemic were also discussed. These insights can inform targeted, context-specific strategies to improve HPV vaccination rates and reduce cancer disparities.

title: The impact of fungal infections on the course of disease in patients with COVID-19: a prospective observational study
abstract: Objective: to analyze the manifestations of fungal complications in COVID-19 and their impact on the course and outcome of the disease, taking into account comorbid pathology. Materials and methods: the types of fungal complications were studied in 118 adult hospitalized patients with COVID-19. The comparison groups consisted of 23 patients who died with fungal complications, 35 patients who died without fungal complications, 35 patients who recovered with fungal complications, and 25 patients who recovered without fungal complications. Results: it was established that the presence of fungal flora worsens the course of COVID-19 and is associated with an unfavorable prognosis. The timing of diagnosis and the location of the pathogen isolation are key: the detection of a fungal infection in the third week and later is significantly associated with a fatal outcome. Candidemia (the isolation of fungi from sputum) is an unfavorable prognostic sign, requiring instrumental monitoring and the prescription of antifungal therapy. Risk factors for developing fungal complications include age over 60, chronic cardiovascular and respiratory diseases, hypothyroidism, cancer, and HIV infection. Fungal pathogens are predominantly Candida albicans (96.6%). A combination of fungal and bacterial infections, particularly P. aeruginosa, MDR Acinetobacter, K. baumannii , is a prognostic marker for an adverse outcome. Conclusion: the data obtained support the need for early mycological monitoring in patients with COVID-19, especially those with risk factors, to promptly identify fungal complications and initiate appropriate therapy, which can significantly improve the prognosis.

title: Characterization of Post-COVID-19 Conditions in People with Obesity: A Scoping Review
abstract: COVID-19 is associated with the persistence and onset of clinical manifestations after the acute phase of infection, characterizing post-COVID-19 conditions. People with obesity may be more vulnerable to complications and persistent alterations related to the infection. In this context, this study aims to characterize post-COVID-19 conditions in people with obesity by identifying the main signs, symptoms, and clinical manifestations described in the literature. A scoping review of the literature will be conducted to map and synthesize the available evidence on the topic. The findings are expected to contribute to expanding knowledge about these conditions and supporting nursing care and healthcare for this population.

title: Future Jobs for People with Disabilities Post-COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: Abstract Technology was the driving force behind future employment for people with disabilities and created opportunities, but it posed challenges regarding the gap between PWD and people without disabilities. Driven largely by the expansion of remote and hybrid work, current employment rates for PWD saw remarkable gains, even outpacing those of nondisabled workers in some sectors. The call of post-pandemic RTO mandates could erode the progress in flexibility of work and technology achieved by PWD in term of progress in the labor market during the pandemic in the United Kingdom and United States. In both countries, the legal framework encourages this kind of flexible working as a potential reasonable accommodation/adjustment, though the United Kingdom had implemented more explicit, universal rights to request it. The second half of the chapter examines the role of AI as a potential to enhance future work opportunities for workers with disabilities in both the United Kingdom and the United States through advanced assistive technologies and flexible work options. However, the realization of this potential could heavily be contingent on proactive policy and regulatory frameworks in each country to address inherent biases in AI-powered hiring tools and government systems. The post-pandemic labor market offered some potential for positive change, largely driven by technological shifts. However, despite the opportunities, the economic situation in many LMICs stayed the same or even worsened. In many of these countries the lack of robust, disability-inclusive policies and social safety nets would make individuals with disabilities vulnerable to economic shocks.

title: Employment for Persons with Disabilities in the Twenty-First Century Before, During, and After the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: Abstract Prior to the pandemic, both the United Kingdom and United States saw increasing employment rates for people with disabilities, driven by policy shifts, strong economies, and rising self-reporting of disabilities. However, significant employment gaps persisted, and workers with disabilities often faced inequality in pay, opportunities, and workplace accommodations. There was a steady increase in the number of people with disabilities who worked in the United Kingdom between 2013 and 2019. However, the gap between disabled and nondisabled people narrowed, but a substantial disparity remained. Despite improvements, workers with disabilities still faced notable inequalities. They were more likely to be in part-time work and lower-skilled occupations. Prior to the pandemic, employees with disabilities were more likely to face discrimination, leading to lower wages, fewer opportunities for advancement, and a lack of necessary accommodation. Employment for people with disabilities in the United Kingdom and United States had seen significant shifts in the twenty-first century, particularly shaped by the COVID-19 pandemic. While pre-pandemic efforts showed some progress, the pandemic temporarily reversed trends before accelerating new opportunities, most notably the expansion of remote work. For workers with disabilities in Low-Middle-Income-Countries (LMICs), the COVID-19 pandemic amplified preexisting systemic disadvantages. While the pandemic caused widespread job loss, workers with disabilities, who were already disproportionately in the informal sector, suffered more severe economic impacts. Post-pandemic, recovery has been uneven, with some progress seen through remote work, but the employment gap persists.

title: Neurocognitive Impact Post-COVID-19
abstract: This chapter analyzes the cognitive effects of COVID-19, particularly post-COVID-19 symptoms such as brain fog, memory deficits, and executive dysfunction. Many individuals experience lingering cognitive impairments due to the neurological impact of the virus, inflammation, and prolonged hospitalization. The chapter discusses emerging research on post-COVID-19 cognitive rehabilitation, including cognitive training exercises, lifestyle modifications such as diet and physical activity, and neurological recovery strategies. The importance of early intervention in mitigating long-term cognitive deficits is emphasized, along with the role of psychological support in addressing mental fatigue and cognitive distress. By integrating rehabilitation programs with medical and psychological interventions, individuals recovering from COVID-19 can improve cognitive functioning and overall quality of life.
journal: Neurocognitive Interventions in Mental Health Practice

By integrating rehabilitation programs with medical and psychological interventions, individuals recovering from COVID-19 can improve cognitive functioning and overall quality of life.

title: Unraveling the Effects of SARS-CoV-2 on Dementia: A Comprehensive Study
abstract: Since late 2019, a pandemic caused by SARS-CoV-2, a highly contagious coronavirus, has jeopardized human and public health. Neurodegeneration and structural brain diseases produce dementia, which is developing rapidly. Strong evidence of COVID-19 brain abnormalities as neurotrophic viruses impair neurological systems. Neuron and glial cell degeneration can affect nerve transmission and brain function. Damage to these brain components raises dementia risk. Multiple studies linked SARS-CoV-2 to dementia. This manuscript contains selective data. This study aims to review the findings and suggest strategies to improve SARS-COVID dementia management. The study makes use of medical research databases like Google Scholar, PubMed, Medline, and Embase. Furthermore, information is also collected by recognized health organizations and government agencies. COVID-19 can produce neuropsychological deficits, agitation, confusion, inattention, and disorientation. Thus, SARS can worsen dementia and neurodegeneration. This article summarizes COVID-19's effects on dementia patients from several sources. The focus on existing treatments for affected patients ties the two.

title: Severe Pediatric Neurological Manifestations with Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children (MIS-C) Linked to COVID-19 Pandemic: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Introduction: Since December 2019, COVID-19 has caused global health challenges. Among pediatric populations, SARS-CoV-2 infections have led to severe multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C), often accompanied by neurological complications. Objective: This study aimed to assess and characterize the neurological manifestations of MIS-C in pediatric patients with COVID-19. Methods: A retrospective cross-sectional cohort study was conducted on 303 pediatric patients admitted to a pediatric intensive care unit in Upper Egypt between March 2020 and March 2023. Patients were divided into three groups: Group I (MIS-C, PCR-positive), Group II (MIS-C, serologypositive), and Group III (non-MIS-C, PCR-positive). Neurological symptoms, laboratory markers, and outcomes were analyzed. Results and Discussion: Neurological manifestations were most frequent in Group II (53.5%), followed by Group I (45.0%) and Group III (14.3%). Convulsions, decreased consciousness, headaches, and weakness were significantly more common in Group I. Inflammatory markers (CRP, D-dimer, ferritin, and troponin) were elevated in Groups I and II. Radiological abnormalities were infrequent, and neuroimaging findings showed no significant intergroup differences. Hospital stays were longest for Group I (mean 7.8 days), and mortality was highest in Group I (21.7%). Severe neurological symptoms correlated with adverse outcomes. Conclusion: This study emphasizes the high prevalence of neurological symptoms in pediatric patients with COVID-19-associated MIS-C, especially in those with positive serology. Symptoms like convulsions, decreased consciousness, headaches, and weakness were more common, with severe cases linked to elevated ferritin and D-dimer levels and abnormal neuroimaging findings. It highlights the importance of thorough neurological assessments in these patients and calls for further research into the long-term neurological effects of COVID-19 in children.

title: Nasal Vaccine: A Special Prominence on SARS-CoV-2
abstract: Nasal administration of mucosal medications and vaccines is an alternate and promising method of drug and vaccine delivery. Mucosal pathways can be used selectively for various disorders due to many benefits. Many initiatives are now being made to yield effective medications and cutting-edge nasal delivery systems. The structure of the nasal cavity and key features were discussed in this review. With a focus on vaccine distribution, the benefits, successes, and difficulties of using the nasal route for medical purposes were examined. The strong result supports the benefits and security, of the safety of nasal medication and vaccination administration. This alternate path may help many unmet medical needs and may also make big vaccination drives or expensive, protracted chronic therapies possible. Today, despite some lingering criticism, the area of nasal medicine and vaccine delivery is expanding quickly, supported by recent advancements in nanotechnology, imaging, and administration devices. The variety of drugs that have been licensed for nasal delivery is expected to increase significantly.

title: Covid-19 and the Entertainment Industry: A Test of Market Efficiency
abstract: The World Health Organization (WHO) declared the COVID-19 outbreak a global pandemic on March 11, 2020. This study examines how the entertainment industry’s stock market reacted to the announcement and tests semi-strong form market efficiency. The pandemic significantly disrupted entertainment markets as lockdowns and restrictions on public gatherings forced the closure of cinemas and live entertainment venues. In response, companies shifted toward on-demand content and streaming platforms, while demand for digital entertainment, including streaming services and video games, increased substantially. Companies such as Netflix and Disney experienced significant growth as consumers remained at home. However, the broader financial impact of the pandemic created uncertainty and substantial pressure across industries. Using standard event-study methodology, this study analyzes risk-adjusted stock price returns for ten major large-cap entertainment companies surrounding the WHO announcement, with day 0 representing March 11, 2020. The event window spans day -30 to day +30. Results support the semi-strong form of the Efficient Market Hypothesis (EMH) and indicate that the entertainment industry experienced a significant negative effect during the event period.

title: Evaluating U.S. Federal Zoonotic Records Against National One Health Goals: A Multi-LLM Assessment Across COVID-19, Monkeypox, and H5N1
abstract: (1) Background: Zoonotic diseases require coordinated action across human, animal, and environmental health sectors. While substantial research has focused on outbreak prediction, forecasting, and surveillance, less attention has been given to systematically evaluating how One Health principles are reflected in government policy documents. (2) Methods: We developed a multi-large language model (LLM) framework to evaluate 477 U.S. government documents covering COVID-19, monkeypox, and highly pathogenic avian influenza (H5N1). Agency technical guidance and Federal Register documents were evaluated using a 19-item rubric covering three goals of the U.S. National One Health Framework: coordination and communication, outbreak response, and surveillance. Claude, GPT, and Gemini independently evaluated the documents. Inter-model agreement and human validation were assessed, and sensitivity analyses examined alternative chunk-to-document aggregation thresholds and the potential influence of document length. (3) Results: One Health alignment was generally limited, with no disease × document-type × goal combination exceeding 39%. Document type showed the clearest differences, with agency technical guidance showing approximately 13–31 percentage-point higher alignment than Federal Register documents across the three goals, while differences across diseases were less consistent. Sensitivity analyses supported the main document-type pattern across alternative aggregation thresholds and after restricting Type B documents by length. After excluding one wording-sensitive rubric item, the three LLMs reached unanimous agreement in 87.1% of document-item evaluations, with human–model agreement (Cohen’s κ = 0.513–0.692) comparable to human–human agreement (κ = 0.649). (4) Conclusions: This study introduces a purpose-built policy corpus and structured multi-LLM evaluation framework for examining how One Health principles are reflected in government documents. The clearest differences were observed across document types rather than diseases, and the main findings were generally stable across alternative analytical assumptions. Together, these findings extend zoonotic-disease research beyond outbreak prediction and surveillance toward systematic evaluation of One Health policy alignment.

title: Organizational Culture and Firm Performance under Environmental Volatility: The Case of the COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: We examine how organizational culture influenced firms’ financial resilience during the COVID-19 pandemic. To investigate the relationship between culture, culture change, and financial resilience in the context of a widespread exogeneous crisis, we use qualitative data from millions of employee reviews on the Glassdoor platform and employ natural language processing (NLP) techniques to estimate over 1,000 firms’ cultural profiles. We provide insights on how six theoretically derived organizational culture dimensions—adaptability, results-orientation, detail-orientation, integrity, collaboration, and tightness—influenced companies’ financial resilience during the COVID-19 pandemic. Our findings advance theory linking culture and culture change to financial resilience as well as explain how culture can buffer firms from the negative effects of exogenous shocks. We also highlight practical insights on how firms can leverage culture to build resilience.

title: Placental trophoblasts exhibit iron dysregulation and ferroptosis signaling associated with SARS-CoV-2 restriction
abstract: Prenatal SARS-CoV-2 infection is associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, but mechanisms shaping placental viral spread and injury remain unclear. We show that SARS-CoV-2 induces ferroptosis-linked iron dysregulation in the placenta as a potential attempt to limit trophoblast infection. Placentas from early gestation infection exhibit persistent viral protein expression, iron accumulation, disrupted iron transport protein localization, and reduced expression of the ferroptosis inhibitor glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) at term. In trophoblast cells and stem cell-derived trophoblast organoids with apical-out polarity, SARS-CoV-2 Delta infection suppresses the iron efflux transporter ferroportin and ferroptosis inhibitors GPX4 and phospholipase A2 group VI (PLA2G6), promoting ferroptotic signaling. Pharmacological activation of ferroptosis reduces viral titers in trophoblasts, supporting a potential antiviral role during infection. Together, these findings identify a possible mechanism through which the placenta restricts SARS-CoV-2 levels. However, this response is accompanied by placental iron sequestration that may compromise maternal-fetal iron transfer, highlighting a delicate balance between iron and ferroptosis-mediated protection and damage.

title: A within-host-informed event-time framework linking epidemiological delay distributions
abstract: Understanding when and how pathogens spread from person to person is fundamental to characterizing transmission, interpreting surveillance data, and designing effective control measures. Yet key epidemiological delays -- including the latent period, incubation period, generation interval, and serial interval -- are difficult to estimate because key events such as infection, infectiousness, symptom onset, and transmission are rarely observed directly. Current approaches typically estimate these delays using flexible statistical distributions rather than explicitly linking them through the underlying processes that generate them, making it difficult to interpret the underlying biology and to ensure consistency across related delay estimates. Here, we develop a stochastic event-time framework built around a dynamic within-host pathogen-growth model that treats epidemiological delays as coupled outcomes of a shared biological process. By representing these key events as linked stochastic events, the framework produces internally consistent delay distributions while inferring parameters with mechanistic interpretations conditional on the assumed within-host model that govern pathogen growth, clearance, infectiousness, and symptom onset. The framework also accommodates censored and partially observed infection and symptom-onset times through a unified observation model. Across simulation studies, the framework accurately recovered generation-interval characteristics across sample sizes and disease time scales. In applications to SARS-CoV-2 and mpox transmission-pair data, the framework showed improved predictive fit relative to conventional lognormal delay models in several analyses, although the magnitude of improvement varied across datasets and observation models; it estimated shorter generation intervals for Omicron than Delta and revealed alternative within-host parameters compatible with the mpox transmission data. This mechanistic framework provides a biologically interpretable alternative to independently fitted delay distributions, yields internally consistent estimates of epidemiological delays, and establishes a foundation for integrating biological and epidemiological data to better understand, predict, and control pathogen transmission.

title: Effects of COVID-19 on Food Supply: A Systematic Review
abstract: Objective: The COVID-19 outbreak has had a significant influence on several critical industries, including agriculture, education, and the economy. This essay investigates these processes, with a focus on agriculture, where the repercussions have been particularly harsh for poor groups dealing with unpredictable food supplies and food safety. Methods: Along with a critical examination of the shift to digital education systems, the report highlights the major obstacles that lie ahead for regions lacking adequate digital infrastructure and digital literacy. There have been notable disruptions in the economy as well. Manufacturing, the financial markets, and tourism have all seen major downturns. Results and Discussion: The study emphasizes the crucial part that following safety measures and boosting immunization campaigns play in mitigating these negative consequences while supporting economic recovery. Also, new technical solutions have emerged throughout this time. The application of drone technology to contactless food delivery is a notable illustration of how creativity can overcome the challenges posed by the pandemic. Conclusion: Finally, the report recommends the development of specific and rigorous methods to strengthen recovery efforts in these critical areas.

title: The well-being of small-scale farmers post-Covid-19 pandemic: A mediation-effect approach
abstract: Small-scale farmers are vulnerable to unpredictable threats, including climate disasters, price volatility, and health shocks. While the first two hazards occur frequently, farmers experienced both health crisis and market shock simultaneously during and post COVID-19 pandemic. Leveraging unique information of 461 rural households collected in the Vietnamese Mekong Delta in 2023, this research investigates the extent to which the COVID-19 pandemic hit farming household welfare as measured by income. Hence, the impacts of COVID-19 infection were analysed through two alternative proxies: (1) households with at least one infected member before vaccination; and (2) households’ perceptions of COVID-19 seriousness. The findings reveal that household income was largely negated by the COVID-19 pandemic irrespective of the proxies used. Quantile regression models uncover that the COVID-19 infection hit wealthier households harder than those in lower income groups, whereas the perception of COVID-19 seriousness had more negative influences on the lower tail of the income distribution. Further, the mediation analysis model exhibits that the pandemic directly reduced household welfare and hampered on-farm diversification in household income as a mediator. Hence, this study provides useful insight into the effectiveness of the recovery policies and the preparedness for future inevitable dangers, especially in rural communities.

Hence, this study provides useful insight into the effectiveness of the recovery policies and the preparedness for future inevitable dangers, especially in rural communities.

title: Alterations in Liver Function Biomarkers Among Moderately Severe COVID‐19 Patients in southeastern Serbia: A Retrospective Single‐Center Study
abstract: Liver biochemical abnormalities have been reported in nearly half of patients with SARS-CoV-2 infection. Aim of the study was to determine the prevalence of altered liver biomarkers (ALT, AST, LDH, GGT, and albumin) in COVID-19 patients with a moderately severe clinical picture at hospital admission, and to assess the presence of altered liver-related biomarkers in the absence of a severe clinical presentation. Research material consisted of medical histories of patients with moderately severe clinical picture of COVID-19 who were hospitalised at the Clinic for Infectious Diseases of the University Clinical Centre in Niš. The study included 655 patients (425 male and 230 female) that were divided into three groups: patients without comorbidities (NC), patients with arterial hypertension (HTA), and patients previously diagnosed with diabetes mellitus (DM). Additionally, within each research group, patients were divided into three age subgroups: patients aged 20-40 years, 40-60 years, and over 60 years. AST, ALT, and LDH showed statistically significant differences across the defined groups, while GGT did not. Logistic regression confirmed increased odds for elevated AST and LDH values ​​in all older and comorbid groups, with the most pronounced effects for LDH. For ALT, significantly increased odds were observed among patients with HTA (40–60 years) and DM (40–60 years). The most pronounced changes were observed in elderly patients and those with hypertension and diabetes, with LDH emerging as the most sensitive, although non-specific, biomarker, likely reflecting systemic inflammation and disease severity in addition to possible hepatic involvement.

title: Patterns of recorded sexual violence in Lithuania before and during the COVID-19 pandemic: A national registry-based repeated cross-sectional study.
abstract: Sexual violence is a major public health and medico-legal concern, but many cases remain unreported. During the coronavirus disease 2019 pandemic, social isolation, restricted services, and psychosocial stress raised concerns about changes in reporting. This study aimed to analyze and compare patterns of officially recorded sexual violence in Lithuania before and during the pandemic. A retrospective, registry-based, repeated cross-sectional study used data from the Departmental Register of Criminal Offences on recorded sexual offenses in Lithuania during 2018 to 2021. Cases were divided into pre-pandemic (2018-2019) and pandemic (2020-2021) periods. Data were analyzed using Microsoft Excel and R 4.3.2 with Rcmdr 2.9.2 (R Foundation for Statistical Computing). Categorical variables were compared using chi-square or Fisher exact tests, with Monte Carlo simulation where appropriate; quantitative variables using the t-test or Mann-Whitney U test; and population-based recorded case rates using Poisson rate comparison. A total of 736 recorded sexual violence cases were analyzed. Recorded cases decreased from 451 before the pandemic to 285 during the pandemic, and the recorded case rate decreased from 8.01 to 5.07 per 100,000 population (rate ratio 0.63, 95% confidence interval 0.54-0.74, P < .001). Rape was the most frequently recorded offense type. Most recorded victims were female, and most cases involved suspects known to the victim. The proportion of minors among recorded victims slightly increased, but not significantly (64.8% vs 69.0%, P = .255), while the population-based recorded victim rate among minors decreased. Victims were significantly younger than suspects (P < .001). Recorded alcohol involvement slightly decreased, but not significantly. Among cases with documented physical-damage information (48.1%), non-severe health impairment was recorded more frequently during the pandemic period (3.95% vs 18.08%, P < .001). In Lithuania, officially recorded sexual violence cases and their population-based rate decreased during the coronavirus disease 2019 pandemic, while the main recorded victim-suspect profile remained broadly similar. Most recorded cases involved female victims and suspects known to the victim, and minors constituted a large proportion of recorded victims. Among cases with documented physical-damage information, non-severe health impairment was more frequently recorded during the pandemic period.

title: Discovery Of An Antiviral Protease Inhibitor From Cytosorb Desorbate (Identification of SPINK1 from CytoSorb Desorbateas a Novel Antiviral TMPRSS2 Inhibitor)
abstract: TMPRSS2, a host serine protease, activates the SARS-CoV-2 Spike and is a validated antiviral target.We asked whether the desorbate of used CytoSorb hemoadsorption cartridges, an underexplored clinical matrix, is a source of protease inhibitors.Desorbed material was enriched by trypsin-affinity chromatography (trypsin as a TMPRSS2 surrogate), fractionated by RP-HPLC, and screened for antiviral activity against SARS-CoV-2 Spike pseudoparticles.The active fraction was identified as full-length SPINK1 by MALDI-TOF/PSD.Recombinant SPINK1 inhibited TMPRSS2 (IC50 ≈ 134 nM) and blocked XBB.1.5Spike-mediated entry (IC50 ≈ 562 nM) dose-dependently, establishing hemoadsorption desorbates as a viable discovery matrix for bioactive protease inhibitors.

title: Dexmedetomidine: A Promising Agent to Enhance Tolerance of Non-invasive Ventilation in COVID-19 Patients: A Narrative Review
abstract: COVID-19 patients can exhibit a hyperinflammatory response, which may result in acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and hypoxemic respiratory failure. While the effectiveness of non-invasive ventilation (NIV) for treating COVID-19 patients with ARDS is not well established, many clinicians still opt for this treatment. Patient intolerance is the primary factor limiting the use of NIV, highlighting the need for sedative agents. Dexmedetomidine (Dex), an α2 adrenergic receptor agonist, is used as a sedative and anxiolytic medication. Unlike other sedatives, Dex does not act through the GABA pathway, so it does not depress the patient's respiratory drive. This drug also exhibits antioxidant effects and modulates the inflammatory system, making it potentially more appropriate for hyper-inflammatory states in COVID-19 patients. Despite the studies, our knowledge about the choice of sedative agents in this condition remains limited. This narrative review aims to provide information about the role of sedative agents, particularly Dex, in COVID-19 patients undergoing NIV. We conducted a literature search to examine the mechanisms of the human immune response to COVID-19, the immunomodulatory effects of Dex, and how this agent can enhance the acceptance of NIV among COVID-19 patients. The beneficial effect of Dex with antioxidant and immunomodulatory mechanisms has been shown in various studies. While there is a significant amount of research regarding the role of Dex in non-COVID patients undergoing NIV, studies focusing on COVID-19 patients are limited and primarily consist of case reports and retrospective observational studies. Nevertheless, the findings suggest that Dex may help improve the tolerability of NIV. Dex not only reduces agitation and delirium but also enhances the acceptance of NIV treatment. Due to its immunomodulatory and antioxidant effects, it can be considered a viable option for improving patients' respiratory status. However, future interventional studies are essential to understand better the efficacy and safety of Dex in severe COVID-19 patients.

title: Societal values versus individual rights with respect to public health related practices during the COVID-19 pandemic in the U.S.
abstract: Policies aimed at limiting COVID-19 spread during the pandemic generated dissatisfaction and resistance as they limited privileges or were perceived to infringe on individuals’ rights. Simultaneously, pandemic control and risk mitigation practices are seemingly subject to social resistance, just as other personal risk mitigating practices like seat belt use are. This analysis contributes to understanding U.S. resident perceptions of and compliance with public health pandemic control measures in January 2021. resident agreement with societal values statements as they pertain to healthcare, societal obligations to protect the elderly and children, and individual rights were studied. For all personal viral spread reducing behaviors studied, likelihood of participation increased with increasing agreement that: healthcare is a human right; the respondent wears a seat belt; we have a societal responsibility to protect the elderly; and having themselves or someone in their household in the higher risk group for COVID-19 complications. Agreement that gun ownership was a right decreased the likelihood of participation in any of the personal behaviors that affect viral spread. This study aims to understand societal perceptions of individual responsibility and rights relative to societal values and responsibilities, which has implications for future public health policy discussions.

title: Social disparities and the COVID-19, influenza, and RSV ‘tripledemic’ in Ontario, Canada: A population-based study
abstract: Abstract We examined inequalities in weekly hospitalization rates related to COVID-19, influenza, and respiratory syncytial virus based on neighbourhood-level material deprivation, neighbourhood-level ethno-racial diversity, rurality, and sex. Hospitalization rates were measured as the weekly number of hospitalizations per 10 000 people. Local regression models were used to fit observed weekly hospitalization rates within each study year and each population subgroup, and statistical significance of between-subgroup differences in peak hospitalization rate was assessed based on the overlap of 95% confidence intervals. We also provided comparisons of pre-pandemic (July 2017–June 2020) versus post-pandemic (July 2020–June 2023) trends. More materially deprived neighbourhoods showed up to a 2.5-times increase in peak weekly hospitalization rates compared to less materially deprived neighbourhoods. Peak hospitalization rates were up to 2.3-times higher among more versus less diverse neighbourhoods. Some age groups showed peak hospitalization rates up to 2.8-times higher among urban residents. Peak hospitalization rates were up to 1.3-times higher in younger males versus younger females and up to 1.6-times higher in older females versus older males. Variations due to neighbourhood-level material deprivation, neighbourhood-level ethno-racial diversity, rurality, and sex should be considered when designing and implementing public health policies aiming to reduce respiratory virus burden.

title: Supporting the psychosocial well-being of patients with Long COVID: patient-informed strategies from a qualitative study
abstract: Long COVID, an illness characterized by long-lasting symptoms following SARS-CoV-2 infection, exacts a substantial toll on psychosocial well-being and overall health. Persistent physiological symptoms and associated experiences can negatively impact employment, daily functioning, identity, and social relationships. However, there is a gap in the literature on patient-derived recommendations for addressing the psychosocial impacts of living with Long COVID. This study aimed to identify factors shaping the psychosocial well-being of individuals with Long COVID and elicit patient-generated strategies for addressing them. We conducted semi-structured individual interviews and Community Advisory Team (CAT) focus groups between November 2024 and June 2025 with 19 individuals who self-reported experience with Long COVID. Interviews and focus group meetings were recorded, transcribed, and qualitatively analyzed to identify factors influencing psychosocial well-being and participant-generated strategies for addressing them. Three primary factors negatively influencing patient psychosocial well-being were identified: identity disruption , isolation , and uncertainty . Identity disruption was described as a combination of shifting capabilities and a loss of self-reliance. Isolation centered around reduced social participation and experiences being dismissed, doubted, or misunderstood. Uncertainty focused on the illness and treatment pathways, navigation of healthcare and disability systems, fluctuating symptoms, and an uncertain life trajectory. Participants identified strategies including case management, structured peer support, Long COVID awareness campaigns, and personal practices supporting adaptation and acceptance. Effectively treating and supporting Long COVID patients requires consideration of their broader state of psychosocial well-being and how it is influenced by identity disruption, isolation, and uncertainty. The impact of interventions targeting these specific factors should be studied to guide future intervention implementation.

title: Influence of IL10 promoter variants rs1800896 (-1082 A > G), rs1800871 (-819 C > T), and rs1800872 (-592 C > A) and haplotypes on COVID-19 symptom presentation in outpatients from Western Mexico
abstract: Interleukin-10 (IL-10) is a key immunoregulatory cytokine whose expression is influenced by genetic variation within its promoter region. Altered circulating IL-10 levels have been associated with COVID-19, highlighting its relevance in modulating host immune responses during SARS-CoV-2 infection. This study aimed to evaluate the association of IL10 promoter variants rs1800896 (−1082 A > G), rs1800871 (−819 C > T), and rs1800872 (−592 C > A), haplotypes, and circulating IL-10 concentrations with the clinical presentation of COVID-19 in Mexican outpatients. A case–control study was conducted in 179 Mexican outpatients with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection, including symptomatic cases and asymptomatic controls. IL10 promoter variants (rs1800896A>G, rs1800871C>T, and rs1800872C>A) were genotyped using PCR-RFLP, and serum IL-10 levels were quantified by ELISA. Haplotype analyses were estimated, and their associations with clinical symptoms were assessed. No significant differences in genotypic or allelic frequencies of rs1800896A>G or rs1800871C>T were observed between symptomatic and asymptomatic individuals. In contrast, the rs1800872C>A genotype (codominant model) and the combined CA+AA genotypes (dominant model) were significantly more frequent among asymptomatic participants, conferring protection against symptomatic infection (aOR = 0.52; 95% CI: 0.28–0.97). Haplotype analysis revealed a higher frequency of the ACC haplotype in symptomatic patients (aOR = 1.68; 95% CI: 1.01–2.79), who also exhibited higher circulating IL-10 levels than GCC carriers (1.018 vs 0.564 pg/mL). Although overall IL-10 concentrations did not differ significantly between groups, elevated levels were observed in individuals reporting anosmia (1.026 vs 0.515 pg/mL) and ageusia (1.186 vs 0.606 pg/mL), whereas lower levels were detected in those with pharyngitis (0.59 vs 0.939 pg/mL). Variability in the IL10 promoter particularly the rs1800872 C>A variant and the ACC haplotype, was associated with symptom presentation and with haplotype-specific circulating IL-10 levels during SARS-CoV-2 infection.

Although overall IL-10 concentrations did not differ significantly between groups, elevated levels were observed in individuals reporting anosmia (1.026 vs 0.515 pg/mL) and ageusia (1.186 vs 0.606 pg/mL), whereas lower levels were detected in those with pharyngitis (0.59 vs 0.939 pg/mL). Variability in the IL10 promoter particularly the rs1800872 C>A variant and the ACC haplotype, was associated with symptom presentation and with haplotype-specific circulating IL-10 levels during SARS-CoV-2 infection.
